Where do Antrim County property records live, and how far back do they go?

Deeds, mortgages and liens on Antrim County land are filed with the Register of Deeds at the county building in Bellaire, which keeps a grantor and grantee index and serves weekdays from 8:30 to 5:00. The register also chairs the County Plat Board, the body that reviews new subdivisions before they can be sold off in lots.

Antrim's own office page says its filings reach back to 1856. Computer images start in January 1990, and older entries sit in bound books. The name index covering the whole life of the county can be searched without charge at a public terminal, though you reserve a slot by appointment.

The register's page also explains why timing matters. Michigan runs a race-notice system, so a recorded deed puts every later buyer on notice, and the office stamps and numbers each paper in the order it lands on the counter. A lake cottage that changes hands in July should have its deed filed the day the money moves.

What does the Antrim County fee schedule list for recording?

Antrim charges a flat $30.00 for each document it records, whether the deed runs one page or twelve. The county fee schedule adds a few other items that matter at a sale.

  • When one paper handles more than one assignment or discharge, add $3.00 for every instrument past the first.
  • Warranty deeds, any deed carrying a covenant of warranty, and land contracts (plus assignments or amendments that touch the legal description) need a $5.00 treasurer's certificate.
  • Photocopies cost $1.00 a page, plat copies $2.00 a page, and a certified copy costs $5.00 for its first page.

The office accepts a check, cash or a credit card. Make checks out to the Antrim County Register of Deeds, and expect the certificate to be handled through the treasurer's window.

Charges listed on the Antrim County Register of Deeds fee schedule
ServiceAmount
Record a deed, mortgage or lien$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Tax certificate (County Treasurer)$5.00
Copy of a recorded paper$1.00 per page
Copy of a plat$2.00 per page
Certified copy$5.00, first page

How much transfer tax comes due on an Antrim County sale?

The tax is charged per $500 of the price, with any leftover fraction counted as a full block, and it is paid at recording. Other Michigan register offices post a state share of $3.75 per block plus a county share of $0.55, which adds up to $4.30. Antrim's office can confirm its county share.

As a worked example, Census figures for 2020 through 2024 put a typical owner-occupied Antrim home at $255,500. That price spans 511 blocks, so the combined tax would be about $2,197. Your own bill follows the real sale price on the deed.

The state act lists transfers that owe nothing. The exempt group in MCL 207.526 includes:

  • a gift deed running to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild;
  • transfers by foreclosure or by a deed in lieu of foreclosure;
  • court orders that move title without naming a money amount;
  • a quitclaim that repairs a title flaw by confirming what the grantee already holds;
  • any instrument where the price is below $100.

The deed text itself must name the exemption claimed, or the office will collect the tax.

Can an Antrim County deed be filed electronically or dropped off?

Yes to both. The register recommends e-recording through Simplifile or EPN, and still accepts the post office, FedEx, UPS and similar carriers. A drop box at the southeast corner of the county building takes hand deliveries, but the office says it is only checked periodically, so a deed on a closing deadline should go another way.

Slip a return envelope with postage into anything you mail, and the original comes back once it is indexed. Staff can say what a filing needs, yet drafting a deed or picking a form is outside their role.

At a normal sale none of this lands on the seller. The closing agent signs the deed with you, adds the transfer tax and the treasurer's $5.00 certificate, and sends the package in electronically. Owners handling an inherited cabin by hand can call the office before they file.

Which office bills property tax in Antrim County, and how is an old balance paid?

Your village or township bills the year in progress. The County Treasurer takes only earlier years and delinquent accounts. Summer bills go out in July and are due to the village or township on September 14. Township winter tax is billed in December and due February 14.

To pay a past-year balance, the treasurer accepts a check by mail at PO Box 544, Bellaire, MI 49615, a card online or by phone at 231-533-6720, or a visit to the secure drop box outside the public entrance. Card payments add 2.95 percent, with a $3.99 minimum. The treasurer's page also points to the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services for people who may qualify for help.

If the parcel carries an unpaid balance, call the treasurer for a payoff figure before the house goes on the market. The closing agent deducts that sum from what you receive.

What should a seller know about Antrim County's land and housing?

Antrim covers 602 square miles of northwest lower Michigan, and 126 of them are water. Torch Lake, which Wikipedia calls the deepest and second-largest inland lake in the state, lies here, and most of the Chain of Lakes does too. Grand Traverse Bay marks the western edge, and Bellaire is the seat.

Five villages anchor the map: Bellaire, Central Lake, Elk Rapids, Ellsworth and Mancelona. Alba, Alden, Eastport and Lakes of the North are census-designated places. A shoreline lot at Elk Rapids and a woodland house near Mancelona sit in different markets, so get comparable sales from the immediate area.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 24,698, a gain of 5.4 percent over the 2020 estimates base.
  • Owner-occupied homes: 86.4 percent of 11,100 households.
  • Median household income: $72,054 in 2020 to 2024 dollars.
  • Residents 65 or older: 30.7 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 105.
  • Median gross rent: $902 a month, and median owner cost with a mortgage: $1,462 a month.
  • Average household size: 2.15 people.

Many houses in the county are seasonal or came through an estate, and a place closed up through several winters can need roof, plumbing or septic work before a financed buyer will go ahead. A buyer who takes the house in its current condition skips that repair list, and that draws some owners to a cash sale.

More questions about Antrim County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing fee for an Antrim County deed?

The fee is $30.00 for a document of any length. Each extra assignment or discharge on the same paper adds $3.00, and warranty deeds and land contracts also need the $5.00 treasurer's certificate.

Does the Antrim County office take deeds by e-recording?

Yes, through Simplifile or EPN, which the register encourages. Paper still works by mail, by carrier, or through the box at the building's southeast corner.

Which office collects this year's tax on an Antrim County house?

The village or township holds the current year's tax roll. The county treasurer steps in for prior years and delinquent bills, and the due dates for summer and winter township tax are September 14 and February 14.

Will the register's staff prepare my deed?

No. They can describe what the office needs, but writing the deed is left to a preparer you hire. Heirs and sellers working without a closing agent should line one up first.

Is a deed to my daughter taxed as a sale in Antrim County?

MCL 207.526 exempts a parent's conveyance to a child from the state tax, provided the deed names the exemption in its text. The county side has its own wording, so confirm the exact language with the register before you sign.

Why would an Arenac County seller deal with the Register of Deeds?

The deeds office in Standish files the paper trail of Arenac County real estate: deeds, mortgages, discharges and the other instruments that move or burden land. For a seller, it is the office that turns a signed deed into a public record, and it is also the counter where state and county transfer tax get collected. You can reach the office at (989) 846-9201.

Its web page invites owners to sign up for land notifications, an alert service that sends an email when a new document is recorded against a property. A person who inherited a house, or who owns a place that sits empty for part of the year, may want that watch in place before listing.

Arenac is small. It is the third-smallest county in Michigan by land area, and the register's workload follows: an estimated 9,615 housing units spread along the Saginaw Bay shore and the inland river valleys.

What are Arenac County's recording charges?

Every document filed in Arenac County pays $30.00, however many pages it has. The county cites MCL 600.2657 and says the flat fee took effect on October 1, 2016.

When one document assigns or discharges more than a single instrument, the office adds $3.00 for each instrument beyond the first. A payoff release that clears two recorded mortgages, for example, would cost $36.00 to file.

ChargeRate
Recording any document$30.00 flat
Each added instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 or fraction
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or fraction
Transfer tax applies when the value is$100 or more

What would transfer tax run on an Arenac County house?

Add the county's 55 cents to the state's $3.75 and a sale pays $4.30 per $500 of price, with a leftover partial $500 counted as a whole one. The middle-priced owner-occupied home in Arenac County was valued at $150,600 in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates. That is 302 blocks of $500, so the tax would come to $1,298.60. Your sale will be taxed on its own price.

The register's page lays out the paperwork. The deed should show the property's value. A real estate valuation affidavit can be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says an affidavit is being filed. The statutes the office cites for this are MCL 207.511 and 207.525.

  • The office collects the tax unless the deed qualifies for a state exemption, a county exemption, or both.
  • The deed has to name the exemption, with the statute behind it (MCL 207.505 for the county, MCL 207.526 for the state).
  • Exemptions under the state act reach gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure transfers, and deeds that only confirm title the buyer already holds.

Can you search Arenac County deeds online?

Yes, with two separate tools. The county's online records site covers documents from February 11, 1991 forward, and it lets you search and buy copies of filings from 1992 to the present. Older index books are handled differently.

For anything before 1992, the office points researchers to RECORDhub. You make an account, pick one of the subscription plans Arenac County offers, and then view and print pages from deed books 1 through 214. That archive is how a family finds the chain of ownership on a farm or a lakeshore lot that has not changed hands for decades.

Online searching tells you what is on file, but it does not replace a title search. If a seller spots an old easement, a lien or a name that does not match the deed, a title company can sort out what it means before a buyer's lender does.

Who handles property tax bills in Arenac County?

Ask the treasurer of the city, village or township where the parcel sits for the current tax bill, and ask the Arenac County Treasurer about any amount that has fallen behind. Each can give you a written figure to hand the closing agent.

At a sale, an unpaid tax balance is normally paid from the seller's side of the closing statement. On an older or inherited house, request the payoff early, so the number you plan around matches the one the closing agent sees.

Arenac's register does not handle tax collection, so questions about assessments or exemptions go to the local assessor or treasurer rather than to the deeds counter.

How do Arenac County's geography and past shape a house sale?

Arenac County covers 681 square miles, and 47 percent of that is water, mostly Saginaw Bay on Lake Huron. Standish, the seat, is the largest of three cities along with Au Gres and Omer and Sterling, Turner and Twining as villages. The county has a start-and-stop past: the Michigan Territory created it in 1831, it was attached to Saginaw County for administration in 1836, and the creation of Bay County legally erased it in April 1857. It came back on April 21, 1883, carved from Bay County's northern townships. Anyone tracing an old Arenac farm deed should expect the records to reflect that history.

Several rivers cross the county, including the Au Gres, the Rifle and the Pine. I-75 and US 23 are the main routes, along with M-13, M-33, M-61 and M-65. Off-reservation trust land of the Isabella Indian Reservation sits in three small parcels inside Standish Township.

  • Population estimate for 2025: 15,068, a rise of 0.5 percent over 2020.
  • Households: 6,552, with 86.2 percent in owner-occupied homes.
  • Median household income: $58,811, and median gross rent: $761.
  • People 65 or older: 30.0 percent of residents.
  • Residential and other building permits in 2025: 43.

Against a median home value near $150,600, repair costs weigh heavily on a sale. A place needing a roof, a furnace or a cleanout may suit a cash buyer who accepts it as it stands.

What does the Arenac County economy look like around a house sale?

Arenac County is a place of small employers and long commutes. The Census Bureau counts 355 employer establishments with 3,619 workers in 2023, a gain of 6.9 percent over 2022, and an annual payroll of about $169 million. Workers who travel to a job spend a mean of 26.6 minutes getting there.

The shoreline adds a visitor trade. Accommodation and food service sales came to roughly $128.6 million in 2022, and retail sales reached about $268 million, or $17,724 for each resident. For a seller, that background matters mostly at the margins: buyers who want a getaway near Saginaw Bay and buyers who need a year-round home bring different budgets.

  • Residents past age 25 holding at least a high school diploma: 88.2 percent, and holding a four-year degree: 16.0 percent.
  • Persons in poverty: 11.7 percent.
  • Per capita income: $32,082, in 2024 dollars.

More questions about Arenac County, MI Register of Deeds

How do I contact the Arenac County deeds office by phone?

The office lists (989) 846-9201 on its web page. Call that line with questions about recording, transfer tax or the online records subscription.

What does a deed filing cost at the Arenac office?

A deed pays $30.00 whatever its length. A paper that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each one beyond the first.

What are the Arenac County transfer tax rates?

The county takes 55 cents per $500 and the state takes $3.75 per $500, rounded up for a partial block. A transfer worth $100 or more owes both unless the deed states an exemption.

Do I have to put the sale price on the deed?

Not if you file a real estate valuation affidavit instead. There is no fee for the affidavit, and the deed must say that one is being filed.

Where can I look at old Arenac County deed books?

Deed books 1 through 214 can be viewed on RECORDhub with a subscription plan from the county. Documents from 1992 forward are on the county's online records site.

Barry County by the numbers

Where do you take a deed in Barry County, and what is staff allowed to help with?

Go to Room 102 at the Barry County Courthouse, 220 W State Street, Hastings, MI 49058. The office posts Monday to Friday hours from 8:15 to 4:45, shuts for the noon hour, and answers at 269-945-1289 or bcrod@barrycounty.org. Its page offers a useful reminder: filing a deed puts it in the public record without vouching for its legality.

Clerks record, index and preserve what arrives. They do not search titles, hand out blank forms or coach anyone on wording, so the deed itself comes from your closing agent or a lawyer. Nothing already on file can be altered, and a name added to or dropped from ownership means a brand-new deed gets signed and filed.

People sometimes ask for the "title" to a house. The county answers that most homes have none, since the recorded deed covers whatever is permanently fixed to the land. Certain mobile homes are the exception and may keep a separate title with the Secretary of State.

What are the Barry County recording charges, and who pays what?

A flat $30.00 covers any document, and each added instrument number that a paper assigns or discharges brings another $3.00. Sale deeds and similar transfers owe state and county transfer tax on top, collected during recording. One payment to the Register of Deeds can cover the fee and the tax together.

One item travels separately. Land contracts, their assignments, warranty deeds and any deed with a warranty covenant require a Tax Certification from the Barry County Treasurer, priced at $5.00, written as its own check to the treasurer.

Barry County charges posted on the register's recording and FAQ pages
ItemAmount
Recording a document$30.00
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3.00
Tax certification (check to Treasurer)$5.00
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 or fraction
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 or fraction
Copy by mail or email$1.00 per page, plus $5.00 search fee if no document number

The counter takes cash, checks, and debit or credit cards; cards add a small service fee.

What transfer tax goes with a Barry County sale?

In the register's FAQ, the seller carries the tax, set at $4.30 for every $500 of consideration, and it is due the moment the deed is recorded. Take $264,100, the 2020 to 2024 Census median for homes in Barry County. It holds 529 blocks of $500 after rounding up, so the tax lands at $2,274.70.

Some transfers escape the tax, though staff will not choose an exemption on your behalf. A deed claiming one must show MCL 207.505 (county) or MCL 207.526 (state) plus the exemption's letter, and the county posts separate lists for each. Have your closing agent make that call.

  • Family gifts to a son, daughter or grandchild sit among the state exemptions.
  • Foreclosure transfers, and deeds given to avoid foreclosure, are exempt from the state tax.
  • Deeds that fix a title flaw by confirming what the grantee already owns are exempt, along with any instrument priced under $100.

The full state list sits in MCL 207.526.

What does the Barry County office require on a deed?

State statutes set recording standards, and Barry posts a checklist drawn from them. Run through it before filing. These are the main points from the county's page.

  • Ink signatures in black or dark blue, original rather than copied, with each name typed or printed under it.
  • An acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary in Michigan, with the notary's name typed on the signature page.
  • A street or post office address for each grantee, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A blank 2.5 inch strip at the top of page one, and half an inch of white space around the rest.
  • Readable black print no smaller than 10 point, on white 20 pound paper sized from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • The property's full value stated in the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit attached.
  • A certified death certificate recorded alongside, or ahead of, any deed that conveys by survivorship.

Photocopies are rejected. Court orders must carry the clerk's seal, and all other documents need original signatures.

What are the ways to file in Barry County, and when does the paper come back?

Walk it in, mail it, or route it through an e-recording company. Barry names five: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, Nationwide Title Clearing, EPN and CSC. A document sent by ordinary email is not recorded.

A paper that meets the standards is recorded the day it is received, according to the FAQ, and walk-in filers take the recorded copy home. Mail and drop-offs usually return in 2 to 4 business days. Enclose a stamped return envelope, or the office keeps the original for 90 days at least. Digital PDF returns through Swift are free and arranged with staff.

One catch from the county's page: the treasurer issues electronic tax certifications only via Simplifile and CSC. Confirm that your closing agent's provider fits before signing day.

Does the register handle property tax or foreclosure questions?

Property tax is outside the register's job. Its FAQ points owners to the city or township for current bills and to the Barry County Treasurer for delinquent amounts. If the parcel has back tax, get a payoff figure from the treasurer first.

Foreclosures reach the office only after the sale occurs, so staff cannot say whether a house is set for sheriff's sale. After a sheriff's deed is recorded, the office takes the redemption payment but does not compute it. Open liens show up in a title search, run at the public workstations or through a title firm.

For ownership questions the county suggests starting with its GIS property map. It follows the tax roll and shows the listed taxpayer, while the recorded deed settles who actually owns the parcel.

What is Barry County like for a seller?

The county spans 577 square miles, 553 of them land. Hastings serves as its lone city and its seat, with Freeport, Middleville, Nashville and Woodland as villages and Delton, Dowling and Hickory Corners as census-designated places. Where is the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?

The Charlevoix County Register of Deeds sits at 13513 Division Street in the city of Charlevoix, MI 49720. The state treasury list of registers of deeds gives the phone as 231-547-7204 and the fax as 231-237-0106, and the office takes email at rod@charlevoixcounty.org. Call before you drive in, because the office page does not post public counter hours.

The city of Charlevoix is the seat, while Boyne City is the largest city. Anyone selling a house here, whether it is a Lake Charlevoix cottage, a place in East Jordan, or a home on Beaver Island, finishes the transfer at this one office. The county Register of Deeds page describes the office as a constitutional office created in 1835 that records, indexes and preserves land documents.

What happens to my deed once Charlevoix County receives it?

Staff stamp the time on it, give it a liber and page, scan it and add it to the searchable index. That sequence is what puts the buyer's name on the public record for the property.

The office is plain about its limits. Its page says recording does not make a document legal; it makes the document public. Counter staff have no blank deed forms to hand out and cannot draft or coach, because MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from legal advice. The deed itself comes from your closing attorney or the title agent, and the register of deeds only checks it against the recording rules.

  • Deeds, mortgages, land contracts and discharges are recorded here.
  • The computer image index reaches back to January 1984, and older records are still being indexed.
  • Documents can be walked in or mailed with the fee and a prepaid return envelope.

What are the Charlevoix County recording charges?

Filing one document costs $30.00 whatever its length. That amount follows MCL 600.2567, and the county fee page notes that $4.00 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund.

Charlevoix County Register of Deeds statutory fees (county fee page)
ItemCharge
Recording one document$30.00
Each extra liber and page on an assignment or discharge covering several instruments$3.00
Tax certification$5.00
Copies of documents$1.00 a page
Plat copies$4.00 a page
Certified copy$5.00

One check payable to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds can cover the recording fee, any transfer tax and the tax certification together. Since January 2, 2025, the office adds $3.00 per document for return postage when you send a document in without a prepaid return envelope, and it holds the document unrecorded until that amount arrives.

What transfer tax comes due at a Charlevoix County closing?

Most sales carry two taxes, both counted in $500 slices of the price with any leftover treated as a full slice. MCL 207.504 sets the county rate at 55 cents a slice for counties under 2,000,000 people. MCL 207.525 puts the state rate at $3.75 a slice.

Take a sale at $276,800, the Census median value for homes that owners live in here. That is 554 slices, so roughly $305 in county tax and $2,078 in state tax. The full value has to appear on the deed itself, or an affidavit stating it travels with the deed.

Some transfers escape the county tax. MCL 207.505 lists instruments with consideration under $100, security instruments such as mortgages, leases, and deeds that only fix a title flaw. Check with the office on how your own deed is treated well before the closing date.

Which layout rules can bounce a deed at the Charlevoix counter?

A deed must satisfy the page rules in MCL 565.201, and the office may not take one that misses them. Formatting causes most returns, so inspect the sheet before it goes in the mail.

  • Margin: 2.5 inches of clear space at the head of page one and half an inch around the rest of every page.
  • Print: 10-point type or bigger, black ink, white paper of 20-pound stock or heavier.
  • Size: letter or legal sheets only, from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • First line: one statement naming the recordable event, such as warranty deed.
  • Only one recordable event per instrument.

The statute also wants a legible printed name under every signature that matches the acknowledgment, and the name and workplace address of whoever drafted anything signed after 1964.

Why do I need a tax certificate before a warranty deed is recorded in Charlevoix County?

Michigan law makes the office ask for proof that no tax liens attach to the parcel. Under MCL 211.135 the county treasurer certifies that taxes for the five years leading up to the deed date are paid, and Charlevoix charges $5.00 for that certification.

The county fee page names the deeds that trigger this step: warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts, and trustee, fiduciary or personal representative deeds with a warranty clause. It reaches master deeds for condominiums as well. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants is excluded by MCL 211.135(6)(e), so it moves through without the certificate. Start at the County Treasurer's Office first, then bring the certificate with the deed.

How can I search records or guard my title in Charlevoix County?

The county offers three search routes and a free fraud alert. Webtecs is the free portal for taxpayers and occasional users, and images can be bought document by document. Laredo Anywhere is a subscription service for people who run title searches regularly, and the office asks for an email to rod@charlevoixcounty.org to request an agreement. Tapestry is a web search that needs no subscription.

Homeowners can also enroll in Property Fraud Alert, which sends the owner an alert whenever a filing appears under their name. That helps after a sale too, since a seller can watch for a deed or lien appearing against a property they believed they had cleared.

How does Charlevoix County's housing stock look in federal data?

Charlevoix County is one of the pricier corners of northern Michigan. The Census Bureau counts 26,036 residents in 2025 and 18,026 housing units. Owners live in 83.5% of occupied homes, median rent is $949, and the typical household brings in $76,531 (five-year survey ending 2024).

In the 2020 count, 35.4% of housing units sat vacant, which points to plenty of seasonal and second homes. Builders took out 111 permits in 2025. Water covers 70% of the county's 1,390 square miles, and the 416 square miles of land make it the fourth smallest county in Michigan by land area, so waterfront parcels and island properties often carry details that the deed and title search have to capture accurately.

What is the filing charge for one deed in Charlevoix County?

One document costs $30.00 whatever its length. A tax certification adds $5.00 when the deed type calls for one, and a mailed document with no prepaid return envelope adds $3.00 for postage. Transfer tax is separate and follows the sale price.

Can the Charlevoix County office prepare my deed for me?

No. Staff cannot draft papers or give legal advice, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from it, and the office keeps no blank deed forms. Have an attorney or the title agent prepare the deed first.

Do I need a tax certificate for a quitclaim deed in Charlevoix County?

Usually not. MCL 211.135(6)(e) exempts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty from the certificate rule. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds, land contracts and certain fiduciary deeds do need the County Treasurer's certification first.

How do I pay the transfer tax on a Charlevoix County sale?

Pay when you hand in the deed. The fee page asks that transfer tax and tax certification checks be made out to the Charlevoix County Register of Deeds, and one check can cover them together with the recording fee. Rates are 55 cents (county) and $3.75 (state) per $500 slice.

Search the free Webtecs portal and buy the image, or ask the office. The fee page lists plain copies at $1.00 a page and certified copies at $5.00, so request the exact total on a long document.

A deed carrying warranty promises needs county treasurer certification first. MCL 211.135 asks for proof that the parcel's taxes are paid for the five years ahead of the deed date, plus a statement of any tax liens or titles.

Subsection (6)(e) excuses a quitclaim deed that has no warranty covenants, and subsection (6)(c) excuses a sheriff's deed from a court proceeding. If a deed is presented after March 1 and before the local treasurer has filed the current delinquent tax return, the certificate carries a note that the return was not available, and the register of deeds may not refuse the deed for that reason alone.

What formatting mistakes get a Cheboygan County deed rejected?

Mismatched names, missing addresses and cramped signature blocks cause most trouble. MCL 565.201 sets the rules that every Michigan register of deeds applies.

  • Each signer's name is printed beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, and matches the name in the acknowledgment.
  • A notary's name is printed or stamped on the same page near the notary signature.
  • Every grantee's address appears on the deed, using the street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The person who drafted it is named, with a workplace address.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number are removed or obscured.

A deed written in another language needs an English translation attached. A returned deed goes back to your drafter for repair.

What should a Cheboygan County seller know about the local housing picture?

Cheboygan County is big, thinly settled and full of seasonal homes. Its 885 square miles split into 715 of land and 170 of water, and the Census Bureau counts 35.8 residents per square mile.

The 2025 estimate is 25,793 people, and 30.6% of them are 65 or older. Owners hold 85.6% of homes, the middle rent is $773, and the typical household earns $62,875 (five-year survey ending 2024). The 2020 count found 36.0% of the 17,631 housing units vacant, and the Census lists 74 building permits for 2025. County government was organized in 1853 after a merger with the former Wyandot County.

How do I protect my Cheboygan County property from deed fraud?

Sign up for Property Activity Alert, a service that watches for recordings under your name. The office explains that it cannot stop fraud, but the alert warns an owner early so they can act. Call 231-627-8866 and the staff will enter your name and email address.

This is useful for sellers who keep another parcel in the county, and for anyone who inherited land and has not yet recorded a transfer into their own name.

More questions about Cheboygan County, MI Register of Deeds

When can I reach the Cheboygan register of deeds counter?

The Register of Deeds window runs Weekdays, opening at 8:30 and closing at half past four. Other clerk services start at 8:00. Closures follow the county holiday list, which includes Good Friday and the day after Thanksgiving.

Can I pay recording fees by card in Cheboygan County?

Yes. Cash, checks and debit or credit cards all work at the office, and most services can be paid by card over the phone. Coin payments above $5.00 are refused.

Is a quitclaim deed taxed differently in Cheboygan County?

A quitclaim deed does not need the treasurer's tax certificate, but transfer tax can still apply if money changes hands. MCL 207.505 exempts deeds that only confirm a title already held, and deeds with consideration under $100.

How is the county transfer tax calculated in Cheboygan County?

Divide the price by $500, round up, and multiply by $0.55. The state tax rounds the same way at $3.75. A $200,000 sale gives 400 steps, so $220 county tax and $1,500 state tax.

Does the Cheboygan office help me write a deed?

No. Hire an attorney or the title agent to draft it. The county posts a general recording requirements sheet and sample warranty and quit claim deed layouts that show what the register of deeds expects.

Where is the Chippewa County Register of Deeds?

Chippewa County is in the eastern Upper Peninsula, and Sault Ste. Marie is the county seat. A seller on Drummond Island, in the Sault, or anywhere along the St. Marys River records the deed here. Mail works as well as a visit, as long as the document, the fee and the return envelope go in together.

How is Chippewa County organized, and who answers tax questions?

Chippewa County government was set up in 1826 and once reached across most of what is now the Upper Peninsula and parts of Minnesota. The Act of March 9, 1843 cut that vast area down, and the county now follows the Canadian border along the St. Marys River. Sault Ste. Marie anchors the Sault Ste. Marie micropolitan area, and Drummond Island is part of the county.

The county itself operates the jail, maintains rural roads, runs the major local courts and keeps the deed and mortgage records. Police, fire, building and zoning, tax assessment and street maintenance belong to the cities and townships. A seller with a question about an assessed value or a building permit therefore calls the local township or city office, not the register of deeds. The register of deeds answers questions about what has been recorded against the parcel, and it can tell you whether an older mortgage was ever discharged on the record before your buyer's lender asks.

  • Recording, indexing and copies: the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street.
  • Assessment and local zoning: the city or township where the house sits.
  • Tax certificates for warranty-type deeds: the treasurer offices named in MCL 211.135.

Why does a Chippewa County house sale end at the Register of Deeds?

Only a recording here puts the new deed into the county's land record. The office also holds the mortgages, discharges and liens that a title agent hunts for when clearing your title.

The online land records system shows how deep the file goes. Its indexes start on May 16, 1865, which gives a title examiner well over a century of names to search. Sellers who inherited a Chippewa County house can use that index to find the deed that put the family on title.

  • Guests search the index free of charge.
  • Members log in with a group, user ID and password, and login charges may apply.
  • PDF copies are bought by credit card after the search.

What do recording and copy charges look like in Chippewa County?

Under MCL 600.2567 the recording fee is $30.00 a document unless a charter county has adopted a different schedule. The same section prices copies at a dollar a page and certifying a recorded document at $5.00.

Five dollars of the $30.00 is set aside for the register of deeds' automation fund. Send payment together with the deed, because the office wants it at the time of filing.

Which Chippewa County deeds escape transfer tax?

MCL 207.505 carves out a list of instruments, and a few of them come up often here. A mortgage or other security instrument is carved out. So is a lease, and so is a deed whose stated consideration is under $100.

  • A deed where the grantor is the federal government, the state or a local government.
  • A deed given to settle, or in place of foreclosing, a government-backed or insured loan.
  • A corrective deed that repairs a defect in title the buyer already holds.
  • A boundary-straightening deed when no money changes hands.
  • A transfer between husband and wife that sets up or dissolves an entireties tenancy.

Everything else owes the county 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 slice. Phone the office to learn which exemption, if any, fits your deed.

For a taxable sale, work it out on paper before closing. A house that sells at $161,900, the Census median value for the county, covers 324 slices of $500. County tax comes to $178.20 and state tax to $1,215.00, which makes $1,393.20 together. The deed has to show the full consideration, or an affidavit with the value goes on top of it, so the clerk can check your arithmetic.

What else must a Chippewa County deed carry besides the legal description?

MCL 565.201 requires details about the people named in the deed, and one missing item stops the recording. Every grantee's address must be printed, using the street number where street numbers are normal and a post office address where they are not.

Any Social Security number must have its first five digits removed or blacked out. A deed in a foreign language needs an English translation stapled on. Anything signed after January 1, 1964 must show who drafted it, with a business address. A notary's printed name belongs on the same page as the notary's signature.

Do I need a tax certificate to record a Chippewa County deed?

For most warranty-type deeds, yes. MCL 211.135 directs the office to demand certification that no taxes are unpaid for the five years preceding the deed, together with a statement of any liens or tax titles on the parcel.

Certificates come from the county treasurer and from the treasurer of the local city, village or township. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants, sheriff's deeds and state tax deeds are among the exceptions. Skipping the step is a misdemeanor for a register of deeds, with a fine up to $100, so the office does not bend on it.

How do Chippewa County homes measure up in the Census data?

By land area Chippewa is Michigan's second largest county, with 1,558 square miles of dry ground inside 2,698 total. It touches both Lake Huron and Lake Superior, and the Census puts density at only 23.6 residents per square mile.

The 2025 estimate is 36,081 people, down 1.9% from the 2020 base. Three of every four homes are owner-held (75.0%), and the middle rent is $797. A typical home is valued at $161,900, and a typical household takes in $62,217. The county has 20,556 housing units, and builders pulled 86 permits for them in 2025. In the 2020 count, 31.7% of units stood vacant and 27.5% of occupied homes were rented.

The state fee under MCL 600.2567 is $30.00 a document whatever the page count. Add transfer tax where it applies and any certification charge the treasurer sets. The office at 906-635-6312 can quote the final total.

Yes. Guests can search the online index at no charge. A PDF of a document is $1.00 a page plus a $5.00 online fee per order, paid by credit card.

The online indexes begin May 16, 1865. The system posts its own index range and upload date on its welcome screen, so you can see how current it is before you search.

Is a mortgage subject to transfer tax in Chippewa County?

No. MCL 207.505 exempts instruments given as security, and an assignment or discharge of them. You pay the recording fee, but not the transfer tax, when you record a mortgage.

Reach the Register of Deeds at 319 Court Street in Sault Ste. Marie, phone 906-635-6312, email rod@chippewacountymi.gov. A question about what the deed should say belongs with an attorney or the title agent.

The Michigan Legislature created the county from part of Michilimackinac County in 1840 under the name Kaykakee County, and renamed it Clare County in 1843. As in other Michigan counties, the county records deeds and mortgages, while cities and townships handle tax assessment, building and zoning, and street maintenance. Ask the township or city office about assessments, and ask the Harrison office about what is on the record.

It records the deed that moves ownership to your buyer and the mortgage that goes with it. The same office holds earlier deeds, land contracts, discharges and liens, so a title search on a Clare County house begins and ends in these books.

Copies run a dollar a page and a certification is $5.00. A requested records search costs 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 floor, and filing some other paper is $1.00. Charter counties may use a different schedule, so verify the total with the Clare office by phone.

The deed must print the total value of the real property, or an affidavit of value goes with it. Both the county act (MCL 207.504) and the state act (MCL 207.525) say so.

With the value printed, the arithmetic is short. The county takes 55 cents and the state takes $3.75 on every $500 slice of price, partial slices counted whole. A $133,800 sale, which matches the Census median home value in Clare County, spans 268 slices: $147.40 for the county and $1,005 for the state. If real and personal property sell together, naming each value separately confines the tax to the real property. Ask the office how it collects the tax so payment arrives with the deed.

What belongs on page one of a Clare County deed?

The first printed line must name the recordable event in a single statement, such as warranty deed or quit claim deed. MCL 565.201 bars recording an instrument signed after April 1, 1997 when that statement points to more than one event.

When does a Clare County deed need treasurer certification?

A deed that conveys title with warranty covenants, and a land contract, needs county treasurer certification under MCL 211.135. The certificate says whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirms payment of the taxes for the five years that precede the deed.

Ionia County by the numbers

Who files the deed after an Ionia County home sale?

The Ionia County Register of Deeds files it. That office keeps the land records for the whole county, and a sale becomes public only once the deed is stamped, indexed and filed there. Staff will not help you draft or repair paperwork, so the papers should arrive complete, drafted by a lawyer or the closing company.

Land area in Ionia County is roughly 571 square miles. The seat is the city of Ionia, and the county counts as part of the Grand Rapids-Kentwood metro area. Filing can happen at the counter, through the mail, or through an approved electronic provider. Counter filings are handed back on the spot. Mailed packets come back only if you include a self-addressed return envelope, and anything sent without one is held 90 days. For questions, call (616) 527-5320 or write deeds@ioniacounty.org.

What will the Ionia County deed filing cost me?

Thirty dollars covers each document, however long. Payment can be cash, check or card, and card payments add a service fee that depends on the amount. One check can cover the filing charge and both transfer taxes.

Ionia County Register of Deeds charges
ItemAmount
Filing a deed or mortgage$30.00 per document
Document that assigns or discharges several instruments$3.00 for each one past the first
Treasurer tax certification (warranty deeds, land contracts)$5.00
Name lookup by staff$5.00
Photocopies$1.00 a page
Certifying a copy$5.00 added

Source: Ionia County Register of Deeds pages on fees and on searching and copies.

How is transfer tax figured on an Ionia County sale?

Ionia County publishes two rates that apply to a deed conveying real estate for money. The state takes $3.75 for every $500 of price, counting any partial $500 as a full one, and the county takes $0.55 on the same basis. A $200,000 price therefore produces $1,500 state tax and $220 county tax, $1,720 combined. That is simple arithmetic on the posted rates; your closing agent will confirm the final number.

Any claimed exemption goes in writing on the deed itself. The two Michigan statutes do not match, and the gap matters for family transfers:

  • MCL 207.526 (state tax) exempts a deed from a parent or grandparent to a child, stepchild or grandchild, along with foreclosure deeds and deeds in place of foreclosure.
  • MCL 207.505 (county tax) exempts instruments valued under $100, security instruments, leases, and court orders that name no price, and it omits the child and grandchild category.
  • Both statutes exempt a land contract until the full contract price has been paid and title passes.

So a gift deed to a daughter can owe county tax while owing nothing to the state. Ask the office how your transfer is classified before you sign.

Which sales need a treasurer certification first?

Warranty deeds, any deed with a covenant of warranty, land contracts, and assignments of land contracts must carry a Tax Certification from the Ionia County Treasurer. The $5 charge can sit on the same check as the filing charge. A quitclaim deed has no warranty covenant, so it usually avoids this step, and the Register of Deeds can say whether yours does.

If back taxes are owed on the parcel, raise it with your closing agent early, because the certification is part of the package that gets filed. Ask the County Treasurer what the office requires before it will issue one.

Why would the office send my deed back?

Clerks check each document against Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201 and related sections. A deed that misses a rule comes back, and a closing can stall for days. The county's own checklist covers the usual trouble spots:

  • Signatures are originals in dark ink, black or dark blue, with each name printed below.
  • The notary block repeats the same printed names, and the notary's name sits on the page that holds the notary signature.
  • The buyer's mailing address appears, as does the drafter's name and address as well.
  • Page one leaves a 2 1/2 inch blank band at the top, with half an inch clear on the remaining edges.
  • The first printed line names the one recordable event the paper covers.
  • Print is black, 10 point or larger, on white stock of at least 20 pound weight, in letter or legal size.
  • A deed to a surviving owner needs a certified death certificate recorded with it or earlier.
  • The full property value is stated on the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit goes with it.

Can I look up Ionia County land records myself?

Yes. Public workstations in the office let you search by grantor or grantee for free, with copies at $1 a page. Searching those machines by legal description or parcel number runs $1 per minute. If you ask staff to find your last deed, the fee is $5 plus copies, and the lookup works by name rather than by property.

Remote searching comes in two forms. Tapestry charges $8.95 per search and suits a single visit. Laredo bills monthly and fits agents, investors and anyone searching often; call the office to open an account. If either service gives you trouble, the county asks that you contact the vendor's support team (Fidlar) first and the Ionia filing counter after that. A title company search digs deeper than either tool when you need the full ownership chain behind your house.

How do Ionia County housing numbers compare for a seller?

Census QuickFacts puts the population at 66,557 in July 2025, slightly under the April 2020 count of 66,804. About 77.3 percent of households own, with a typical owned home worth $198,500 (2020 to 2024 survey years). Typical household income of $75,611 is the highest among the four Michigan counties researched alongside this one.

Commuters average 27.1 minutes each way to work, the longest of those four counties, which fits a county that feeds the Grand Rapids job market. Rent runs $884 a month at the median, and builders pulled only 100 permits in 2025. Resale houses supply most of what buyers see, and your listing joins that pool.

Will the next property tax bill look different after I sell?

A transfer of ownership uncaps taxable value. Under Proposal A, the new figure takes effect in the calendar year after the transfer, so the buyer's bill can climb toward the assessed value. Michigan Treasury posts the Property Transfer Affidavit, Form 2766, which the buyer files with the local assessor. Ask the assessor for your city or township about the filing deadline.

Transfers listed in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act do not uncap. Assessment is a local job in Michigan, handled by the city or township where the house stands, so the assessor there is the person to call about taxable value. Current bills come from that same local unit, and the County Treasurer takes over delinquent ones.

More questions about Ionia County, MI Register of Deeds

Does Ionia County bill by page count?

No. Each document costs $30 to file. Documents that assign or discharge several instruments add $3 for each extra one.

May I email a deed to the Ionia County Register of Deeds?

No. Email filings are refused. Electronic recording runs through accredited servicers named on the county page: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, EPN and CSC. Only a scanned original signed document is accepted.

Who covers transfer tax in Ionia County?

Neither buyer nor seller is named on the county page. Payment comes with the deed at filing, so read your purchase agreement and watch the settlement statement for the amount.

Will paying off my mortgage give me a new deed?

No. Your lender files a discharge of mortgage, which carries the same $30 filing charge, and your original deed remains the proof of ownership.

Is a quitclaim to a relative taxed in Ionia County?

It may be taxed by the county. The state list exempts gifts to a child or grandchild, and the county list leaves them out. The deed has to state the exemption, so ask the office first.

The Resources page of the Iosco Register of Deeds carries three PDFs: a Transfer Tax Chart, a county exemption list and a state exemption list. Ask the office, or open that chart, for the exact dollar amount at your sale price.

Both statutes (MCL 207.505 for the county tax, MCL 207.526 for the state tax) shield some transfers entirely. Examples that come up in house deals:

  • An instrument with consideration under $100.
  • A deed used to confirm a title already held, such as a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A conveyance that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spouses.
  • A deed that creates a joint tenancy when one of the people already owns the property.
  • A transfer in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure of a government-backed or government-made loan under the county act, and any mortgage foreclosure under the state act.

If one fits your sale, the deed has to cite it on its face.

What Michigan filing rules should an Iosco County deed meet?

The state recording statutes, chiefly MCL 565.201 and 565.8, govern the format of every deed, and the Iosco office insists on an original with original signatures. Court orders and death certificates must carry a certified raised seal. Beyond that, county offices across Michigan flag these points:

  • Signatures are typed or printed beneath, and the notary acknowledgment matches those names.
  • The paper lists who drafted it, with name and address.
  • A deed to survivors comes with a certified death certificate on record.
  • A trust agreement that accompanies an instrument is recorded as its own document.
  • Anything in a language other than English has a written English translation attached.

A rejected deed pushes a closing back, so have the preparer check the document against the Iosco office's own requirements page before it goes in.

What are the steps from closing to a filed deed in Iosco County?

Most of the sequence happens before anyone walks into the Tawas City office, and a short checklist keeps the file complete:

  • Have the deed drafted by an attorney or title company, since the office will not prepare it.
  • Sign it in front of a Michigan notary, using original signatures only.
  • Add the tax certification request if the deed has warranty language, with a separate $5 check to the County Treasurer.
  • Calculate the transfer tax from the county chart, or note the exemption on the deed.
  • Submit the deed with a $30 check to the Register of Deeds, adding $3 for each extra cross-reference where one applies.
  • Confirm the filing later through the DoxPop search to see that the document shows up in the index.

The search index reaches back only to the early 1970s, but a deed from this closing will be in it, so a quick lookup afterward confirms the record is complete.

How do I search Iosco County property records?

Search recorded documents through the county's DoxPop link, or visit the office. Staff will not run genealogy searches on your behalf, though visitors may use the records themselves. A Property Watch service from DoxPop sends a notice when a new document is recorded against a property you name.

If you want a copy of your deed, you can get one online or at the counter for $1 a page. Paying off a mortgage does not produce a new deed, since your lender records a discharge and your original deed remains the proof of title.

What is the Iosco County housing picture for sellers?

Of Iosco County's 1,890 square miles, 1,341 are water, which leaves about 549 of land. Most residents live along the US-23 shoreline in East Tawas, Tawas City and Oscoda. The legislature first created it in 1840 under the name Kanotin County, renamed it in 1843, and county government was organized in 1857. Gypsum mining around Alabaster, south of Tawas City, began in 1862 and still operates.

QuickFacts estimates 25,266 people for July 2025, and a third of them (33.0 percent) are 65 or older. It counts 20,221 housing units against only 11,713 households, and the 2020 census found that 41.3 percent of the units were vacant, a sign of the cottages and seasonal houses common here. Owners hold 82.1 percent of the occupied homes. A typical owned home is valued at $142,200 for 2020 to 2024, the lowest of the four Michigan counties studied together here. Rent at the median is $719 a month, household income at the median is $50,066, and builders pulled just 47 permits in 2025.

How will a sale change the property tax on an Iosco County house?

A change of ownership lifts the cap on taxable value the following calendar year, as Michigan Treasury explains in its guidance on Proposal A. The affected buyer files a Property Transfer Affidavit with the local assessor. Which exemptions avoid uncapping is spelled out in section 211.27a(7) of the General Property Tax Act.

Iosco County has an Equalization department and a Treasurer's Office listed among its departments. Ask them how a specific parcel is assessed and billed.

$30, with $3 more for each additional cross-referenced instrument on documents such as mortgage discharges. Copies are $1 a page and certified copies are $5 plus $1 a page.

Do I need a new deed after paying off my Iosco County mortgage?

No. Your lender sends you a discharge of mortgage to record. The deed you received at purchase continues to prove ownership.

Who writes the check for the $5 tax certification in Iosco County?

You do, payable to the Iosco County Treasurer only. Recording fees and copy charges go on a separate check payable to the Iosco County Register of Deeds.

Will Iosco staff add a name to my deed?

No. The office tells people to consult an attorney for that kind of change, because each situation differs. Staff do not prepare documents or give legal advice.

Can I record a photocopied court order in Iosco County?

No. Recording needs an original document with original signatures, and court orders and death certificates have to be certified with a raised seal.

  • Any part written in another language needs an English translation attached.

Two Michigan laws tax real estate transfers: Act 330 of 1993 at the state level and Act 134 of 1966 for counties. The dollar amount at your sale price comes from the Register of Deeds, and the settlement statement will show it.

  • Boundary-line adjustments made without payment.
  • Corrective quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • New joint tenancies where one of the co-owners already had the property.

  • A check for $30.00 to cover the recording, plus $3.00 for each extra liber and page.

  • A return envelope, stamped and addressed, if the package goes by mail.

Selling resets taxable value, according to Michigan Treasury: under Proposal A the cap lifts in the calendar year following the transfer. In Michigan, assessing is largely handled by cities and townships. The local assessor can tell you your taxable value and when the affidavit is due.

Thirty dollars flat per document, with $3.00 added for every extra liber and page reference past the first. When a tax certificate is required, it runs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

The county treasurer's office. Your check for the certificate is payable to the Treasurer, and it must be obtained before the Register of Deeds records a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed.

How do I get my filed deed returned by mail?

How do I reach the Lapeer County Register of Deeds?

Staff serve the public weekdays, opening at eight and closing at half past four. The office page carries a Location Directions link for the street address, and every deed, mortgage and discharge touching Lapeer County land is filed there. Its mission statement promises prompt handling of papers that satisfy the Michigan Recording Act.

Payment can be cash, a check or money order made out to Lapeer County Register of Deeds, or a card used at the counter itself. Title companies and attorneys who file in volume are pointed to Simplifile for electronic submission, and that vendor's help line is 800.460.5657.

A homeowner bringing in a deed should have it signed in dark ink, with each signer's name printed or stamped under the signature, the buyer's street address shown, and the drafter's name and business address on the page.

What are the recording charges at the Lapeer County office?

The flat charge is $30 for each document, however long it runs. A sale adds transfer tax and, for most warranty forms, a tax certificate. The office publishes every figure on one sheet.

ItemChargeAuthority named on the sheet
Entering and recording one document$30.00MCL 600.2567(1)(a)
Each additional instrument assigned or discharged$3.00MCL 600.2567(1)(a)

Which Lapeer County deeds must the treasurer certify first?

The schedule singles out warranty deeds, land contracts, land contract assignments and any deed containing a covenant of warranty. Each one has to be certified by the County Treasurer ahead of recording.

The certificate costs $5, so allow time for that stop ahead of the recording counter. If your paper is some other kind of instrument, ask the treasurer's office whether it also requires one. If the parcel carries unpaid back taxes, talk with the treasurer about what must be cleared before a certificate is issued.

What will a Lapeer County seller owe in transfer tax?

Combined, the two rates come to $8.60 for every thousand dollars of value. Picture a $250,000 house: the county takes $275, the state takes $1,875, and the seller hands over $2,150 at recording.

The instrument must show the full value of the land and buildings, or carry an attached affidavit that gives it. In MCL 207.504 the county rate is written as 55 cents per $500 or fraction, the same thing as the $1.10 per thousand on the local sheet. The Transfer Tax page on the county site links two exemption lists. The county statute, MCL 207.505, excuses several kinds of paper:

  • anything where the money involved is under $100;
  • a mortgage or other security paper, and its later assignment or release;
  • leases, plus land contracts while legal title stays with the seller;
  • a spouse-to-spouse conveyance that sets up or ends ownership by the entireties;
  • a quitclaim that merely fixes a defect in a title already held;
  • a court order moving title with no dollar amount attached.

What happens to the tax bill once the deed is recorded?

Nothing changes automatically. The County Treasurer's FAQ says that office cannot take a name off a bill, so the new owner or the seller has to carry the deed or other proof of transfer to the assessor in the township, city or village where the property lies.

Until the assessor updates the record, the old name may keep receiving the July 1 and December 1 bills from the local treasurer. A bill that goes unpaid after March 1 moves to the county as delinquent, with the 4% administration fee and interest attached, so buyers and sellers should settle who is watching the mailbox before the closing date. Mortgage lenders sometimes miss a payment, and the treasurer's position is that the owner remains responsible for confirming the bill was paid.

Why might a Lapeer County deed be turned away?

A register may not receive a paper that skips the formatting rules in MCL 565.201. The usual causes are small and fixable before you arrive.

  • A printed name that differs from the name in the notary's acknowledgment.
  • Pages with too little white space: the first page needs about two and a half inches clear at the top.
  • Type under 10-point, or ink that is not black on white stock.
  • Full Social Security numbers left visible, when only the last four digits may show.
  • No English translation attached to a foreign-language document.
  • A first line that fails to name the one recordable event the paper evidences.

After a paper is accepted, the law presumes it complies, and a register cannot reject a conforming instrument because of its content.

What other fees can a Michigan register of deeds charge?

MCL 600.2567 allows extras that the Lapeer sheet does not itemize. A name search can be billed at fifty cents for each year covered, with a $5 floor, and any other filing or lookup is $1 per paper.

  • $5 of each $30 recording fee is set aside for the county's automation fund.
  • The statute counts a page as one side of a sheet 8.5 inches wide and 11 to 14 inches long.
  • Foreclosure deeds and forfeiture certificates that a treasurer files can be settled after the sale on a delayed schedule instead of at the counter.

Phone the office before a research trip and ask how a search request would be priced.

How do I guard against deed fraud in Lapeer County?

Enroll in the free email alert offered by the office. Every filing made in a name you list sends a message, so a forged deed or loan against your house gets noticed early.

The office page announces the signup at the top, and a one page form sits on the county website. Sellers should also confirm that the name on their title matches the name they plan to sign, because a mismatch with the acknowledgment is one of the statute's own grounds for refusal.

What is Lapeer County like for sellers?

Lapeer County is one of five counties on the Thumb of Michigan, and it is more rural than Oakland County next door. It spans 663 square miles, with 20 of them water. The Flint River's headwaters sit in Columbiaville.

  • I-69 crosses the county from east to west, while M-24 is the north-south route through the City of Lapeer.
  • M-53 serves Imlay City, and M-90 passes through North Branch.
  • Sanilac, Tuscola, St. Clair, Genesee, Macomb and Oakland counties surround it.

The census counted 52,317 residents in 1970, 70,038 in 1980 and 87,904 in 2000. By 2020 it was 88,619, with an estimate of 89,516 for 2025.

More questions about Lapeer County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the filing fee for a deed in Lapeer County?

Thirty dollars per document, however many pages. A warranty deed adds a $5 certificate from the County Treasurer, and the seller owes transfer tax at $1.10 plus $7.50 for every thousand dollars of value.

What are the office hours for the Lapeer County Register of Deeds?

Monday to Friday, opening at eight and closing at half past four. The Location Directions link on the office page gives the street address.

Is a credit card accepted at the Lapeer County Register of Deeds?

Yes, at the counter only. The office also takes cash, checks and money orders, and checks are written to Lapeer County Register of Deeds.

Who covers transfer tax in a Lapeer County sale?

The seller. The deed shows the total value or has a valuation affidavit attached, and the exemptions under MCL 207.505 apply to the county portion.

Can I be warned if someone records a deed in my name?

Yes. The office runs a free email service that alerts you to any filing under a name you enter.

Where is the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?

The office is at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, in Suttons Bay, and its phone number is 231-256-9682. Email goes to rod@leelanau.gov. The county seat moved from Leland to a site in Suttons Bay Township in 2008.

The Register of Deeds is a constitutional office that dates to Michigan's first constitution in 1835, and Leelanau County has had fifteen registers since 1863. Records go back to that year. Documents received after 4:30 p.m. are held until the next business day, so a deed dropped off late in the afternoon waits for the next business day.

The office records instruments that transfer or encumber real property, and it cannot judge whether a document is legally sufficient or what its author intended. Michigan is a race-notice state, so papers are recorded in the order they are first presented, and first in time is first in line.

What should a seller know about Leelanau County's geography?

The whole of Leelanau County is the Leelanau Peninsula, a triangle of land about 30 miles long that reaches into Lake Michigan from the western Lower Peninsula and is about 25 miles wide at its base. The county's total area is 2,532 square miles, but only 347 of them are land, because 86% of the area is water.

It has the second highest share of water of any county in the country. Lake Leelanau is the largest inland lake, Glen Lake lies inside the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, and North and South Manitou Islands lie within the county line. Part of Traverse City falls inside Leelanau, and Elmwood Charter Township, on the southeastern edge, is the most urbanized piece. The villages are Empire, Northport and Suttons Bay, and ten civil townships cover the rest, including Leland, Glen Arbor, Solon and Centerville. The 2020 census counted 22,301 people, up from 21,708 in 2010.

Leelanau became its own organized county in 1863 and touches other Michigan counties by land only at Grand Traverse and Benzie. Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore was established in 1970. The Grand Traverse Band of Ottawa and Chippewa Indians occupies scattered areas within Suttons Bay Township. Every deed for any of this ground is filed in the Suttons Bay office.

What makes a deed recordable in Leelanau County?

The office accepts only documents with original signatures, and it does not allow digital recording. It has kept the wet ink requirement on purpose, because it has stopped fraud attempts that way.

  • A court document must be certified by the court. A true copy cannot be recorded, and the same applies to a death certificate.
  • Under MCL 565.201 each signer's name is printed, typed or stamped beneath the signature, and the signature is in black or dark blue ink.
  • The notary's name appears on the same page near the signature.
  • Each grantee's street address, or post office address, appears on a deed.
  • The drafter's name and business address appear on instruments signed after January 1, 1964.

The office does not supply forms or give legal help. For drafting it points people to an attorney or title company, and it does not run title searches.

What does recording cost in Leelanau County?

State law sets recording at $30 for any document, whatever its length, and the office accepts cash, checks, debit cards and credit cards. One check can cover recording for several documents, along with transfer tax, a tax certificate and any copy fees.

How do I work out transfer tax on a Leelanau County sale?

Counties of this size levy 55 cents per $500 of value, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. Any leftover fraction counts as a whole $500 unit. Take a $400,000 price: $440 goes to the county, $3,000 to the state, $3,440 overall, due from the seller when the deed is filed.

Leelanau's own guidance adds several points. The deed has to show the total consideration. A Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit may be filed in its place at no charge, provided the deed says so. If land straddles two counties, the price is divided between the parcels and each county is paid its share. Stamps must be purchased in the county that holds the land. An easement is taxable, and a foreclosure instrument carries county tax based on the stated sale price.

Exemptions listed in MCL 207.505 include transfers for under $100, instruments given as security, leases, land contracts that have not yet passed title, spousal conveyances creating a tenancy by the entireties and corrective quitclaims.

How do I search Leelanau County land records?

Use the county's Self Service site, the two public workstations in the Suttons Bay office, or the vault. Names go in last name first with no punctuation, and the search needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year.

  • The free search shows index information only, and each image costs $1.00 per page.
  • Subscription passes run $5 for 15 minutes, $15 for a day, $200 a month and $1,100 for six months.
  • A parcel number search requires the county prefix 45 and the dashes, as in 45-000-000-000-00, and only documents that list the number turn up.
  • Online, only deed records are available before January 1, 1972. Other older records are searched in the office.
  • The historical grantor and grantee indexes went online in October 2025.

Try spelling variants, such as Richard, Rick and Dick, because the office records names exactly as written on each document.

What happens to the record after a payoff, a death or a sheriff's sale?

The office only records, so it does not issue a replacement deed after any of these events. Your original deed stays the deed to the property.

  • After a mortgage payoff, the lender sends a discharge or satisfaction of mortgage. No new deed follows, because the deed was delivered when you bought.
  • When a co-owner dies, bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee. It shows that the deceased person no longer holds an interest.
  • A sheriff's deed is recorded when it is submitted after the auction closes. The office is not the place to redeem; the attorney named on the sheriff's deed handles that.
  • If you have lost your deed, a recorded copy is available at the office, and copy fees apply.

How can Leelanau County owners watch for property fraud?

Subscribe to Fraud Notify, which costs nothing. It sends an email whenever a filing appears under a name you register, and the office has reported several attempts to list owners' property fraudulently that were stopped once owners were told.

If you see a neighbor's lot offered for sale, ask the owner. The office also warns about mail that looks official and charges for copies of your own deed. A 2016 Michigan law set rules for such mailings, and a copy from the office is $1.00 a page.

More questions about Leelanau County, MI Register of Deeds

How can I phone the Leelanau County Register of Deeds?

231-256-9682. The office is in Suttons Bay at 8527 E. Government Center Drive, Suite 105, and also takes questions by email at rod@leelanau.gov.

Does Leelanau County record deeds electronically?

No. The office requires original wet ink signatures and does not allow digital recording, to make deed fraud harder.

What total transfer tax applies to a Leelanau County sale?

The two rates add up to $4.30 per $500 of value, 55 cents for the county and $3.75 for the state. The seller pays when the deed is recorded.

Will Leelanau County record a copy of a death certificate?

Only a certified one. The office will not record a true copy, and it does not issue a new deed afterward, because it only records.

Where can I obtain a copy of my Leelanau County deed?

Go to the Suttons Bay office, ring 231-256-9682 or use the Self Service website. Each page costs $1.00.

Lenawee County by the numbers

Who keeps property records for Lenawee County land?

The Register of Deeds in Adrian, the county seat, receives, records and digitally stores every legal document that affects real estate in Lenawee County. That covers deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens, surveys and land corners. Staff check each item against Michigan's recording rules, record it, and send the original back by U.S. mail to whoever presented it unless instructed otherwise.

Lenawee was carved from Monroe County in 1822 and organized in 1826. It spans roughly 750 square miles of land, counted 99,423 people in 2020 and hosts Adrian College and Siena Heights University. Whether a house stands near Adrian, in Tecumseh or on a farm road in a rural township, the deed goes to this one county office, because Michigan hands assessing, zoning and building rules to individual cities and townships and leaves deed recording with the county.

The 2020 census counted 43,577 housing units in the county, with 11.5 percent vacant and 77.3 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners. One local habit shows up in addresses: in the townships, north-south roads are called highways and east-west roads are called roads, so a newcomer reading a map has to watch which word follows the road name. The legal description in the deed gives the exact boundaries.

The office supplies no forms, and its employees are barred from advising on or helping complete a document. Content and intent are the preparer's responsibility, so closings usually run through a title agent or a lawyer.

What fees apply when Lenawee County records a document?

Recording runs $30.00 per document, whether it is one page or twenty, according to the county's answers to common questions. A page copy at the counter is $1.00. The counter takes checks, cash and cards, and cards carry an access fee.

Owners sometimes receive letters from commercial services offering certified copies of their deeds by mail for as much as $83.00 each. The county flags these and points out that the identical record is available from its own counter for as little as $2.00. Check the county page before paying a mailer.

Which mistakes get a Lenawee County deed bounced?

The county posts 17 statutory requirements and treats them as a minimum, since some instruments carry extra rules. These are the ones that most often matter on a home sale:

  • Signatures must be original, with names typed or printed beneath, and those names must agree with the notary block (MCL 565.201).
  • Page one needs a 2.5 inch blank band across its upper edge, and all remaining edges need half an inch.
  • Use black ink in at least 10-point type on white 20-pound paper that is at least letter size and no longer than legal.
  • The first printed line has to state the recordable event, and one instrument may evidence only one event.
  • Include the grantee's street or post office address, plus drafter identification with a name and address.
  • A Michigan-signed deed needs acknowledgment by a judge, a court clerk or a notary public.
  • Social Security numbers may appear only as the final four digits.

A deed that says "survivor" must be backed by a certified death certificate that is recorded with it or already of record and cited by liber and page. A court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

Is transfer tax owed on a Lenawee County house sale?

On nearly every sale for money, yes. Michigan's state transfer tax attaches to deeds given for consideration. Under MCL 207.523, the seller is the liable party, and the money is paid to the county treasurer for the parcel's location. A separate county transfer tax comes from Act 134 of 1966. Phone the Register of Deeds for the combined figure on your price. Closing agents ordinarily subtract it from the seller's proceeds.

The statutes also list transfers that escape the tax. A few that touch home owners:

  • Deeds with consideration under $100.
  • Gifts of a home by an individual to a child or grandchild (state exemption, MCL 207.526).
  • Court orders that move title without naming a price.
  • Corrective quitclaim deeds that only fix a defect in title.
  • Land contracts, until legal title actually passes.
  • Mortgage foreclosures and the deeds that replace them.

Whichever exemption applies has to be cited correctly in the deed itself, so run the citation past your closing agent.

How can I search land records in Adrian and around Lenawee County?

The county offers an online search with two doors. A text search reads typed or legible text and works on a phone. A second tool serves experienced users and searches by name, recorded date, and liber and page; it runs best on a computer in Chrome or Edge with pop-ups allowed. Results are for information, and document images must be purchased.

Sellers can use the name search to see what stands against the property before listing: the vesting deed, open mortgages, an old lien that was paid but never discharged, or a death certificate that was never recorded. Buyers' title agents run the same search, so a problem found early costs less time.

Anyone worried about deed fraud can enroll in the free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or by phone at 1-800-728-3858. It sends a notice whenever a document carrying the owner's name is recorded.

Where does recording fit in a Lenawee County sale?

It comes last. At closing the title agent collects the signed, notarized deed, pays the recording fee and any transfer tax, and sends the package to the county. Until the deed is recorded and indexed, the sale is not visible in the public record.

Property tax enters the same week. The year after a transfer, the new owner's taxable value is uncapped, and the buyer files a property transfer affidavit with the local assessor. Challenging an assessment starts at the March Board of Review in your city or township and can continue to the Michigan Tax Tribunal, per the county's equalization answers. Owners who need more time on summer taxes are sent by the county treasurer's page to the state's deferment rules.

A house with deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate behind it can sell for cash with no lender repair list. The recording steps are identical in every case, and the $30.00 fee is the same for a one-page quitclaim as for a long deed with exhibits.
