How much is recording in Lenawee County?

The county lists $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. Transfer tax is a separate charge that depends on the sale price.

Can Lenawee County staff draft my deed?

No. Staff do not provide forms and cannot advise on or complete a document for you. Hire a title agent or attorney to draft it.

Who pays Lenawee County transfer tax?

The seller, under MCL 207.523, with payment due to the county treasurer for the property's location. Settlement statements normally show it as a seller charge.

Ask the county office itself. A counter copy is $1.00 per page, and the office says a deed can run as little as $2.00, versus as much as $83.00 from commercial mailers.

Why would a Lenawee County deed be rejected?

Typical causes are photocopied signatures, narrow margins, a missing drafter address, names that differ from the notary block, or type that is too small. Compare the document against the county's 17-point list.

Livingston County by the numbers

Where is the Livingston County Register of Deeds office?

The office sits in the Historical Courthouse at 200 E Grand River Ave, Howell, the county seat. Call (517) 546-0270. The counter opens weekdays at 8:00 a.m. and shuts at 4:30 p.m., with county holidays off.

Most documents never reach the counter. Title companies and attorneys send them electronically through four certified vendors: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A few instruments cannot go that way, including deeds that come with valuation affidavits, plats, and master deeds with large drawings. Those must be brought in or mailed on paper.

Livingston County sits in southeast Michigan along I-96, US 23 and M-59, with 585 square miles of area and a 2020 census population of 193,866. Roughly 86 percent of occupied homes belong to their residents, which keeps deeds flowing through this office steadily. The Census Bureau counted Brighton, Howell and nearby South Lyon as one contiguous urbanized area, and employers such as Tribar, PepsiCo and Citizens Insurance anchor the local economy. Sellers outside those towns, in the rural townships, record at the same counter. The county is laid out in 16 townships of 36 one-mile sections each, which is why legal descriptions on a Livingston deed read as a section number plus a starting corner.

Which fees does the Livingston County office charge?

Every recording carries a flat $30.00 charge, and $4 of it is sent to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. If one instrument assigns or discharges several earlier records, each reference past the first adds $3.

Livingston County Register of Deeds fee schedule from the county FAQ
ServiceFee

Certifying a copy$5.00, all pages must be bought
Tract index use, unless it is your own property$10 per hour

Recording fees and transfer tax are never put on a charge account. Pay with cash, check or card; a card adds a service fee.

How does the office calculate transfer tax?

If a deed states a price, the office takes transfer tax the moment it records. The county describes the total as .086 of the amount, meaning $8.60 per $1,000: $1.10 per $1,000 to the county and $7.50 per $1,000 to the state. The grantor normally bears it. Before the math, the price rounds up to the next $500 step, so $100,000.01 is treated as $100,500.

Applied to a $300,000 price, the total is $2,580. Land that straddles two counties needs the price divided by county on the deed itself.

Exemptions exist. A deed may be exempt from the state share alone or from both shares, never from the county share by itself, and the exemption cited must fit the facts on the page. Mistakes the office sees:

  • Claiming the family-gift exemptions when a trust is the grantor; an individual has to be the grantor.
  • Assuming a church is automatically exempt.
  • Assuming a sheriff's deed escapes county tax. It is always exempt from the state portion, but exempt from the county portion only when the mortgage is federally backed.
  • Citing the under-$100 exemption while the deed shows a $5,000 price.

What does a tax certification cover?

A tax certification is a Treasurer's sticker showing that taxes are paid up and that the legal description matches the township tax roll. It is part of what makes a warranty deed a warranty deed. The county requires it before recording warranty deeds, any deed with "warrant" in the conveyance line, land contracts, assignments of land contract (except those given as collateral), master deeds, and master deed amendments that add property to a condominium.

For a mailed document, enclose the $5.00 and the office gets the certification for you. An e-recorded document that needs one goes through the document router so both departments receive it. The county treasurer's page lists tax clearance of deeds among its duties, so a seller with unpaid taxes learns of it at this stage at the latest.

How do copies, searches and corrections work here?

Searching the index by name is free online. Viewing a page costs $1 plus a convenience fee that covers card processing, and a link arrives immediately. Certified copies, death certificates, tax liens, condo master deeds and documents over 75 pages are mailed after purchase. Records are imaged and indexed back to November 7, 1980 (liber 1000), with earlier books imaged or kept in hard copy.

  • You cannot change a signed, notarized or recorded deed. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed signed by the current owners.
  • When a joint tenant or spouse dies, recording the death certificate shows the survivor as sole owner without a new deed.
  • An enhanced life estate (ladybird) deed becomes proof of ownership once both death certificates are recorded.
  • Paying off a mortgage produces a discharge, not a new deed.
  • A rejected document comes back with a letter listing the reasons, and it can be corrected and resubmitted.

Paper filings by mail or at the counter must come with a return envelope or $3 for postage. Giving an email address instead brings the recorded copy back at no charge, usually the same day.

Can the Livingston County office tell me when my house was built?

No. Deeds describe land and a legal description and rarely say whether a building stood on it, so the office points owners to the city or township assessor. The Howell Carnegie Library reference desk, at (517) 546-0720, can search its archives, and the county Plat Books for 1875, 1895 and 1915 show homesteads and, in 1875, the houses in the towns.

Staff offer one rough method for older homes: a deed whose price is far below a mortgage recorded the same day often marks an owner who was about to build. Name indexes go back to the first recorded documents in 1836 and 1837, and the grantor and grantee indexes reflect documents listed in the tract index. For a sale, a seller who wants proof of a renovation or a permit should ask the local building department instead.

What should a seller verify before the sale closes?

Have the closing agent pull the recorded chain: vesting deed, recorded death certificate if any, mortgage discharges and liens. The Register of Deeds says it cannot verify ownership, since unrecorded land contracts or deeds can affect it, and its staff do not run title searches or give a guarantee. Title companies do that work and can also check probate court records the recorder lacks.

Per the county Equalization Department, the buyer owes the local assessor a property transfer affidavit within 45 days or faces $5 a day in fines, up to $200, and the home's taxable value is uncapped the next year. A seller who knows the taxes will jump for the buyer can say so up front, because it affects what the buyer can afford.

Back taxes, estate paperwork and repair needs are the usual reasons owners ask for a cash sale. Recording works the same whoever the buyer is.

More questions about Livingston County, MI Register of Deeds

What is the Livingston County recording fee?

The flat fee is $30.00 per document, including $4 for the state survey and remonumentation fund. Extra cross-references cost $3 each, and transfer tax is separate.

Who bears transfer tax here?

Usually the seller, who is the grantor. It is collected at recording: $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, using a price rounded up to a $500 step.

Can I record a photocopy of a deed?

No. Only documents with original signatures can be recorded, and even electronic services must scan originals. Court orders, death certificates and surveys must be certified versions.

How do I put a family member on my deed?

Marquette County by the numbers

Where do you take a deed in Marquette County?

Deeds go to the Register of Deeds at 234 W. Baraga Avenue, Marquette, MI 49855, and the counter phone is (906) 225-8415. The county posts weekday hours of 8 to 5. Documents sent through an e-recording vendor can be submitted around the clock, though staff work them between 8 and 4.

The county site traces the office to Michigan's first constitution, in 1835, and spells out why order matters. Michigan runs on a race-notice rule, so whichever buyer records first outranks a later claimant. Documents are processed in the sequence presented, and that is the reason closings tend to record on funding day.

Three desks at the Baraga Avenue courthouse touch most house sales here:

  • The Register of Deeds, for the deed itself, mortgage releases and copies
  • The County Treasurer, at (906) 225-8425, for tax history and delinquent real property bills
  • Equalization and Tax Roll, at (906) 225-8405, for ownership records and parcel maps

What kind of county is Marquette for someone selling a home?

Marquette County is big and thinly settled. It holds 1,808 square miles of land, the most of any Michigan county, with Lake Superior along its north edge and the Huron Mountains inside it. About 47 percent of its 3,425 total square miles is water. The three cities are Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee, and Northern Michigan University, founded in 1899, sits in the county seat.

The Census Bureau counted 66,017 residents in April 2020 and estimated 68,064 by July 2025, which makes this the most populous county in the Upper Peninsula. Federal survey figures for 2020 through 2024 show owners valuing a typical house at $216,500, with 69.6 percent of homes lived in by their owners. Typical gross rent was $949 a month, and a typical household earned $65,429.

The Marquette Iron Range, the Cliffs Shaft Mine and the Jackson Mine are among the ten state historical markers in the county. Parcels near the range towns can have long chains of ownership, so ask your title company how far back it will search.

Which townships and cities make up Marquette County?

Twenty-two local units assess property inside the county, and the county's townships page lists them. Assessing, bills and zoning questions start with the unit where the parcel sits, not with the Baraga Avenue offices.

  • Cities: Marquette, Ishpeming and Negaunee
  • Townships, A to M: Champion, Chocolay, Ely, Ewing, Forsyth, Humboldt, Ishpeming, Marquette and Michigamme
  • Townships, N to W: Negaunee, Powell, Republic, Richmond, Sands, Skandia, Tilden, Turin, Wells and West Branch

Wikipedia's climate table for the county puts January highs near 21 degrees Fahrenheit and lows near 10, with July highs near 68. Allow for that when scheduling a showing or an inspection.

What does a deed filing cost at the Marquette County courthouse annex?

Page count does not matter: one deed is $30.00 whether it runs two pages or twenty. The state remonumentation charge and the register's automation charge are baked into that amount, so the window adds nothing else for the recording.

Charges at the Marquette County recording counter, from the register's schedule of fees
ServiceAmount
File a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Each extra instrument released within one paper$3.00
Treasurer's certificate attached to a warranty deed$5.00
Certified copy stamp$5.00
Ordinary copy, per sheet$1.00
Plat copy, per sheet$2.00
Clerk-run name search$0.50 a year, $5.00 minimum
Copy of a record made before 1983 (county FAQ)$7.50 tract fee added

Transfer tax is separate and applies to any taxable deed. Payment at the counter can be cash, check or card, with a processing charge on cards.

Which part of a Marquette County sale price goes to transfer tax?

The burden sits with the grantor, whoever signs the property over. Marquette County's transfer tax page adds that the deed must state the total consideration. If the price is kept off the deed, a valuation affidavit fills the gap, and the office files it free provided the deed notes that one exists.

Under MCL 207.525 the state portion is $3.75 for each $500 step of the price, with any remainder counted as another step. Take $200,000: 400 steps, so $1,500 for the state alone. Call the office for the county's per-step amount before you finalize a net sheet.

MCL 207.526 exempts some deeds if the grantor says so in the text. Sellers lean on these most:

  • Consideration below $100
  • A deed from an individual to a child or grandchild
  • Transfers following foreclosure, or a deed given to avoid it
  • A land contract that has not yet delivered legal title
  • A corrective quitclaim that only repairs a title flaw

Why would the Marquette County Register of Deeds send a deed back?

Usually the cause is a defect under MCL 565.201. Staff cannot prepare a deed or give legal advice, and only original signatures are recorded, which rules out faxes and photocopies. A "true copy" of a court order is also refused, since the court itself must certify it.

Defects that get a deed returned:

  • Signer names printed under the signatures that disagree with the notary block
  • No mailing address for the buyer, or no name and address for whoever prepared the deed
  • Ink that is not black or dark blue, or type under 10 point
  • Less than 2 1/2 inches of clear space at the top of page one
  • An opening line that names more than one recordable event
  • Full Social Security numbers left on the page

Anything that is not in English needs an English translation attached.

What does the Marquette County Treasurer check before a deed is accepted?

For warranty deeds and land contracts, the treasurer must vouch that the parcel's taxes were paid in each of the five years leading up to the deed (MCL 211.135). Plain quitclaims escape the rule. The treasurer works from the Courthouse Annex, same street address, weekdays 8 to 5, at (906) 225-8425.

On March 1 each year the townships and cities pass their unpaid real property bills up to the county treasurer, and the county then collects them. Debit and credit cards are taken on those delinquent accounts. An owner who is behind can pay before asking for the certificate, or have the title company settle the balance from sale proceeds.

The treasurer's office also sells county plat books and issues tax histories, handy when a buyer wants to see past billing on a parcel.

How can I search or file Marquette County records without driving to Baraga Avenue?

Online, the index and images start with deeds dated January 1, 1980 and with mortgages and miscellaneous papers dated January 1, 1983. Earlier books can be read only at the office.

E-recording runs through CSC, ePN, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile, the four vendors the county names. Some document types cannot go this way, so title companies check with their vendor first, and any rejection is returned electronically.

The register's fraud page cautions about outside companies charging $50 or more for a certified deed copy that the county sells for as little as $1 a page. Owners may also enroll in the free Property Fraud Alert service.

What happens to the Marquette County tax bill after the sale closes?

Recording the deed sets off a taxable value reset. MCL 211.27a gives the buyer 45 days to report the transfer to the local assessor, and the following year's taxable value becomes the state equalized value. The register reports recorded transfers to assessors at least once a month.

The Equalization office studies the county's 22 assessing districts and recommends equalized values to the Board of Commissioners. Its page says it prepares about 50,000 tax statements a year, keeps ownership maps, and warns owners when a defective deed has been recorded. The printed assessment roll sells for $0.15 a page with a $35 minimum.

Before closing, call (906) 225-8405 for a tax code number or parcel map, and ask the local unit what the next bill is likely to be.

More questions about Marquette County, MI Register of Deeds

How much is a flat deed filing in Marquette County?

$30.00 whatever the page count, which already covers the state survey and automation portions. Each additional instrument released in the same paper is $3.00.

Who has to pay the transfer tax in Marquette County?

The grantor, which in a sale is the seller. The state takes $3.75 for each $500 step of the price and the county adds its own amount. A deed to a child or grandchild may be exempt if it says so.

Can I mail a photocopy of my signed deed to the Marquette County recorder?

No. Only originals with live signatures are recorded, and court orders need the court's certification. Phone (906) 225-8415 first to check the paperwork.

Does my Marquette County warranty deed need a certificate from the treasurer?

It does, along with land contracts. The treasurer confirms the preceding five years of taxes are paid, and the fee sheet lists $5.00 for the certification. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

How old are the Marquette County records I can search online?

Deeds from January 1, 1980 and mortgages and miscellaneous papers from January 1, 1983. For older books, visit the office on Baraga Avenue.

What is on file at the Mason County Register of Deeds?

Ask the office for its street address and direct phone line before you send a package.

What is Mason County like, and who is selling homes there?

Ludington serves as county seat and is the biggest city. The county was created in 1840 under the name Notipekago and took its present name in 1843. Of 1,242 square miles, only 495 are land, with the rest under Lake Michigan and inland water. US 10 runs through the middle of the county by way of Scottville and Custer, US 31 meets it close to Ludington, and M-116 follows the lakeshore to Ludington State Park. A piece of the Manistee National Forest falls within the boundary, and Manistee, Lake, Newaygo and Oceana counties are the land neighbors.

The Census Bureau estimated 29,040 residents for 2025, almost unchanged since 2020. Federal survey figures for 2020 through 2024 sketch an older, owner-heavy county:

  • Homeowners report a typical value of $219,600
  • 78.3 percent of homes are lived in by owners
  • Rent for a typical unit comes to $896
  • 28.8 percent of residents have passed 65
  • A typical household earns $64,748

The West Shore Educational Service District, based in Ludington, supports the local school districts, and the county also has a charter school, Gateway to Success Academy, plus Covenant Christian School and Ludington Area Catholic School.

What will the Mason County recorder's counter charge for a deed?

Filing one deed, mortgage or lis pendens is a $30.00 transaction. When a single paper discharges or assigns several instruments, each extra one costs $3.00. Ordinary copies are priced at $1.00 per page, plats at $2.00, and a certification stamp at $5.00.

If staff run a name search for you, the price is 50 cents for every year covered, never less than $5.00, and a state or federal tax lien certificate search costs $3.00 a name. The fee page on the county site shows a February 2018 revision date, so ring the office to verify a figure before you cut the check.

Images and indexes reach back to June 23, 1840 and are online now. Heavy users can buy a prepaid subscription, and occasional users can pay by card per search. The county cautions that its index is a working tool that may contain mistakes and is not a certified search.

How big is the transfer tax bill on a Mason County sale?

The county's table stacks $3.75 of state tax and $0.55 of county tax on each $500 of price, which makes $4.30 per slice. The grantor owes it on any deed given for $100 or more.

The pattern continues beyond the table's top row. A $200,000 sale has 400 slices and owes $1,720, while a $250,000 sale has 500 slices and owes $2,150. For a price that lands between rows, use the county's table.

Separate exemption pages cover the county share and the state share. If one applies, say so on the deed itself. Foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, and land contracts that have not yet passed title are on the exempt list.

What must a deed show before the Mason County Register of Deeds accepts it?

The register publishes the full text of MCL 565.201 as its standard. The short version for a modern deed: legible names under the signatures, the notary's name printed nearby, grantee addresses, and a preparer's name and business address.

Format rules run alongside those. Leave a clear strip about 2 1/2 inches deep at the top of the first sheet, print in 10 point or larger, and stay between letter and legal size. A single recordable event belongs on the first line. A translation must accompany foreign-language text, and most of a Social Security number has to be blanked.

Once the register accepts and records a deed, the law treats it as conforming. A compliant deed cannot be refused because of what it says, so closing agents proof the document before it is presented.

Who certifies taxes on a Mason County deed, and what else does that office do?

The county treasurer. Per the treasurer's page, the office signs off on deeds ahead of recording, confirming nothing is delinquent for the five years before the instrument date, and it hands out tax abstracts on request. Under MCL 211.135 that certificate goes with warranty deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments.

Counter hours are weekdays 8 to 5, and the property tax line is 231 843-8411. Each March 1 the township and city rolls come to the county in a step called settlement, and unpaid real property tax becomes the treasurer's to collect. Village taxes are handled on a different timetable.

Since 2004 Mason County has chosen to run its own tax foreclosures, so the treasurer's staff run title searches, mail notices and sell tax-delinquent parcels instead of the state. The county also opted in to principal residence exemption audits, which means any exemption claimed in error is pursued from the same office.

The board of commissioners has long authorized the treasurer to buy every delinquent real property tax bill. Townships, villages, cities, school districts and special authorities therefore get their full levy in the budget year, and the county recovers the money later as delinquent taxes are paid, sometimes by issuing short-term notes against them.

Which Mason County office handles parcel splits and address changes?

That falls to Equalization, which keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5 and answers at 231-845-6288. The department issues addresses for every unit except Ludington and Scottville, splits and combines tax parcels, takes mailing address updates and supplies aerial and tax maps. Its page also links the county parcel GIS layer, the apportionment report and the yearly equalization report.

Splits come up when a buyer wants only part of a lot or a lakeside piece is being divided. The register records the new deed, and equalization then revises the parcel records.

The register's page also offers owners a free Property Fraud Alert sign-up.

Recording ends at 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, half an hour before the front office closes at 5. A deed handed in late can slide to the next business day, so title agents aim for earlier in the afternoon.

What would transfer tax be if a Mason County house sold for $200,000?

It would come to $1,720: $1,500 for the state and $220 for the county. The seller pays unless the deed states an exemption.

Does a Mason County warranty deed need anything from the treasurer?

Yes. The county treasurer must certify that no taxes are delinquent for the previous five years before the register records it. A quitclaim without warranty language is excused under MCL 211.135.

What is Mecosta County like for a seller?

The county spreads over 571 square miles, 555 of them dry land, and holds more than 100 lakes, rivers and streams. The Muskegon River passes through Big Rapids, the county seat and largest city, where Ferris State University is located. County government was organized in 1859. What does the Mecosta County Register of Deeds charge for recording and copies?

The office also records fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral under the Uniform Commercial Code. All other personal property filings belong with the Secretary of State.

How is transfer tax worked out on a Mecosta County sale?

Two levies add together here. Mecosta County charges 55 cents per $500 slice of value and the state charges $3.75 per slice (MCL 207.525), with any partial slice counted as whole. A deed valued at $100 or more is taxable, and MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor.

Take a $175,000 house: 350 slices, $1,312.50 to the state and $192.50 to the county, $1,505.00 combined. The Register of Deeds office collects both amounts alongside the recording fee, and the act calls for payment inside 15 days of delivering the deed.

The deed has to carry the property's full value. Alternatively, attach a valuation affidavit and add a line on the deed saying it is on file, which costs nothing to file.   • Type under 10 point, or less than 2 1/2 inches of clear top margin
  • An opening line naming more than one recordable event
  • No statement of total property value and no affidavit

Stock should be white and 20-pound, from letter to legal size. Run through the list before mailing, since a rejected package costs days.

Does a Mecosta County deed need a tax certificate?

A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract and an assignment of a land contract all do. The certificate comes from the county treasurer and shows taxes paid for the five years before the instrument date, under MCL 211.135. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

The county treasurer's page describes how unpaid taxes move toward forfeiture and foreclosure, so a seller carrying old bills should ask for a payoff figure before closing. Mecosta County's companion property tax guide covers the summer and winter due dates, the March 1 delinquency date and the appeal calendar.

What do UCC filings and lien searches cost at the Mecosta County office?

The register records only the real-estate side of Uniform Commercial Code work: fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral. A standard-form filing with two debtor names and up to 100 pages is $30.00. Extra charges apply for a non-standard form ($7.00), for filings over 100 pages ($12.00) and for each debtor name past two ($10.00).

  • UCC search, per name: $6.00
  • State or federal tax lien certificate, per name: $3.00
  • Copy of a UCC filing, per page: $2.00
  • Copy of a state or federal tax lien, per page: $1.00

The county notes that its UCC search results cover personal property filings only through June 30, 2001. Real estate filings made after July 1, 2001 appear in the real estate index. Searches are done as time allows and carry no guarantee.

How old are the land records in Big Rapids and the surrounding villages?

The county was set off in 1840 and organized in 1859. The plat of the Village of Big Rapids was recorded on November 3, 1859, and French's addition (Glen Elm) followed on May 9, 1860. The state legislature authorized the City of Big Rapids in April 1869.

Railroads shaped the villages. The Grand Rapids and Indiana line crossed the Little Muskegon River in June 1869, creating the Village of Morley, and construction of the next stretch in late July 1869 brought the Village of Stanwood into existence. The register's documents back to 1859 are imaged, which helps when an old lot line or easement turns up in a title search.

Where can I look up Mecosta County parcels and maps?

The Equalization page links a land records portal and a map viewer, and it carries tax maps for each of the 16 townships: Aetna, Austin, Big Rapids, Chippewa, Colfax, Deerfield, Fork, Grant, Green, Hinton, Martiny, Mecosta, Millbrook, Morton, Sheridan and Wheatland. Its document center also lists the millage rates and a property tax estimator.

Lining up the parcel number on a tax map with the legal description on the deed is a quick way to catch a wrong lot before closing. The Vanguard support line, listed on the register's page, is (888) 608-1808.

Thirty dollars per instrument, plus $3.00 for each additional instrument released in the same paper. Page copies are $1.00 each.

What would a $175,000 Mecosta County sale owe in transfer tax?

$1,505.00 in total, split into $1,312.50 for the state and $192.50 for the county. The seller carries it unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. Phone (231) 592-0148 beforehand to confirm paperwork and payment.

Is an uncertified court order good enough for Mecosta County recording?

No. The clerk of the court must certify and seal it. A plain copy is sent back.

How old are the Mecosta County records that can be searched?

The full index starts January 1, 1968, and papers from 1859 onward are scanned and tagged by liber and page. Countyfusion and Vanguard are the two public portals.

Midland County by the numbers

Where do Midland County deeds get recorded?

The Register of Deeds sits at 220 W Ellsworth Street in Midland, MI 48640, and answers at (989) 832-6820. Recording runs on weekdays, opening at 8 a.m. and closing to new documents at 4 p.m. The vault, where the older books live, opens a half hour later.

A deed that shows up after the 4 p.m. cutoff waits for the next business day, and it queues in the order received as long as cash or a check came with it. The staff take in warranty and quit claim deeds, land contracts, releases, powers of attorney, liens and plats. Drafting and legal advice are outside their role, so a deed still unwritten is a job for an attorney or a title company.

Which fees does the Midland County office list?

A single $30.00 charge covers any document of any length, and the state remonumentation and automation charges are already inside it. The county's own sheet lists a handful of extras.

Fees on the Midland County Register of Deeds sheet

Accepted payment includes cash, checks payable to the Register of Deeds, and cards at the counter, where the card processor tacks on a charge that the office says is generally about $1.50. The office also takes e-recording from qualified submitters, though anything needing a raised court seal or a death certificate has to be brought in on paper.

Which Midland County deeds need a tax certificate first?

Four kinds of instruments, according to the county's recording page, cannot be recorded until the treasurer issues a certificate:

  • A warranty deed, or any deed that includes a covenant of warranty.
  • A land contract.
  • A land contract assignment containing a warranty clause.
  • A master deed for a site condominium.

Order the certificate ahead of closing day. A bare quit claim deed is absent from the list. To see whether a parcel's taxes are current, the county's online lookup offers what the treasurer's counter would show, in the county's words.

What does transfer tax come to under the Midland County chart?

Columns in the county's chart show $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500, so $4.30 together. At a $100,000 price the columns read $750, $110 and $860. Payment is required from a value of $100 upward, subject to the exemption sheets the office links.

The parties may omit the price from the deed by attaching a Real Estate Transfer Tax Valuation Affidavit. A different form, the Property Transfer Affidavit, goes to the assessor for the City of Midland or for the township that holds the parcel, and state law allows the buyer 45 days.

In what order does a Midland County closing move?

A title company runs most of these steps, but the order helps a seller see where the money and paper go.

  • Request a treasurer's tax certificate when the deed contains a warranty covenant.
  • Have the deed notarized. The recorder's staff cannot do it, and the County Clerk in the same County Services Building charges a small fee.
  • Remit both transfer taxes to the county treasurer inside 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523(3)).
  • Record the deed, pay the $30.00, and reach the counter ahead of the 4 p.m. close.
  • Leave the buyer to file the Property Transfer Affidavit with the City of Midland or the township assessor within 45 days.

Recorders also pass a list of recorded transactions to local assessors at least monthly under MCL 211.27a(10).

How old are the records the office holds?

The collection begins in 1855, the year the county was established. Books and microfilm cover the whole run, scanned images with computer indexing start in 1968, and online images reach back to 1950. Searches run through Fidlar-hosted tools called Tapestry EON and Laredo, and recorded papers are public, so anyone can request copies.

The index for 1958 to 1968 is available in an Adobe search format, and entries older than 1958 turn up in the Simple Search option. The office says back-indexing continues, so an older chain of title may need a visit or a call. The county's recording page also links a property fraud alert and a reporting form, which is worth raising with the office when an inherited parcel still carries a relative's name.

What does the ground and water situation look like for sellers?

By Census Bureau measure the county holds 517 square miles of land and two incorporated cities, Midland, the county seat, and Coleman. The Tittabawassee River runs through Edenville Township and past the village of Sanford. In May 2020 the Edenville and Sanford dam failures forced evacuations across parts of the city, the village and several townships, so a seller near the river should expect buyers to ask about flood history. Dow Chemical dates to 1890 in the city of Midland, per the county history.

Service lines vary by location. The city of Midland provides water and sewer to its residents and a few neighboring townships, while parcels beyond municipal water rely on private wells and septic systems. Winters are cold and snowy, with January highs near freezing. Out in the townships, collect well and septic records before listing.

What else do buyers weigh in Midland County?

Buyers looking at a Midland County house tend to ask about the surroundings as well as the structure. The county's profile points to a few answers:

  • Scheduled flights leave from MBS International Airport near Freeland, and Flint's Bishop International Airport is the other option.
  • No regular public bus service exists. Dial-A-Ride covers trips inside the city, and County Connection serves the rest of the county, both for a fare.
  • The Pere Marquette Rail-Trail follows a former rail corridor, with more than 20 miles of riding according to the county's website.
  • Grace A. Dow Memorial Library serves the city and most townships by contract, and Coleman Area Library covers Coleman, Geneva and Warren townships.

The Midland County Educational Service Agency supports the county's districts with special education, early education and career programs. Ask the district office for the boundary that applies to your address, since township lines and school lines differ.

How does Midland County's housing stock compare in the Census data?

The Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 83,754 people living among 37,723 housing units. Renters pay about $1,016 a month, and they occupy roughly 22 percent of homes, which leaves 78.1 percent in owner hands. A 2020-2024 survey values the middle owner-occupied house at $195,400 and puts household income at $77,705. Only 128 building permits were issued in 2025.

Population has crept up 0.3 percent since the April 2020 base. Nine in ten residents lived at the same address a year earlier, a sign of long tenure. Commutes average 23.7 minutes, and 36.6 percent of adults aged 25 and over hold a bachelor's degree.

220 W Ellsworth Street, Midland, MI 48640, phone (989) 832-6820. Recording closes at 4 p.m. on weekdays, and papers received later are recorded the next business day.

$30.00 for any document, regardless of length. A treasurer's tax certificate for a warranty deed adds $5.00 for up to five legal descriptions.

Yes, from qualified submitters, including documents that need tax certification. Paper is still required for documents that need a raised court seal or a death certificate.

Can the register's staff notarize or draft a deed?

No. The office does not write legal documents, and its own staff do not notarize what they record, since that would create a conflict of interest. The County Clerk's office next door has a notary available for a small fee.

What would a $100,000 sale owe in transfer tax?

$860 in total: $750 to the state and $110 to the county, according to the county's chart. A $200,000 sale would owe $1,720 at the same rates.

When can you record a deed in Monroe County?

Monroe County's deeds office takes recordings Monday through Friday between 8:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. A real property document that arrives after 3:00 p.m. is handled on the next working day, so the practical cutoff for same-day posting is an hour earlier than the closing time. Ask the office for its current counter location and e-recording instructions before sending a courier.

Most sellers never visit. Their title agent carries the deed in and pays the charge from the closing funds.

What does Monroe County charge for recording?

Every instrument, whether a deed, a mortgage or a lis pendens, costs a flat $30 however long it runs. The amount already includes the Michigan remonumentation and automation fees. The county accepts cash, checks and credit cards, and a card adds 3 percent, with a floor of $2.

Monroe County Register of Deeds charges that sellers meet
ServiceFee

Certifying a recorded document$5
Real estate copy, per page$1

State tax lien search certificate$1

UCC copies run $2 per page, and a recorded plat copy on letter paper is $1. One exception removes the $3 add-on: a document that moves from the State of Michigan or a local government to a Land Bank Authority.

How is transfer tax computed in Monroe County?

The county's fee page prices the state tax at $7.50 per $1,000 and the county tax at $1.10 per $1,000 of total consideration, so $8.60 combined. Applied to $228,900, the Census median for owner-occupied homes, that is roughly $1,969: $1,717 state and $252 county, before rounding up to the next $500 step.

State law makes the seller liable, with payment due at the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed changes hands. MCL 207.526 exempts several kinds of deeds, among them gifts to children and grandchildren, deeds that simply confirm title, and foreclosure transfers. The county treasurer's office issues the certificate that warranty deeds, master deeds, land contracts and land contract assignments with a covenant of warranty must show under MCLA 211.135.

Can you look up a Monroe County deed by street address?

No. The office searches by name only and asks for a grantor or grantee plus an approximate year. Its staff cannot trace ownership from a street address. A person who lacks the owner's name can obtain the names on the tax roll from the County Equalization Department or a city assessor, though the roll may list someone other than the true owner.

That rule matters when a relative's house is being sold. Before asking a title company to search, collect these items and have the search check for any lis pendens or lien:

  • The earlier deed or deeds in the family.
  • Probate papers, if an estate owned the house.
  • The exact spelling of every owner's name, with the approximate year of each transfer.

Tax lien searches are priced separately: $1 for a state tax lien certificate and $6 per name for a federal one.

Does the office handle commercial filings that touch a house sale?

The fee page also covers Uniform Commercial Code filings, which can surface in a title search. A standard form filing and a termination of a filing each cost $30, and the schedule lists fixture filing fees as not applicable. Its UCC section marks standard-form debt filings, assignments, amendments, continuations and partial releases as not accepted, and the notes say the information on UCC searches runs only through June 30, 2001, because realty-related filings after July 1, 2001 are recorded in the real estate index alone.

The practical lesson is to search the real estate index, not the personal property files, when checking for a lien on a house.

What sets Monroe County apart as a place to sell a house?

It is the only Michigan county touching Lake Erie, and the shoreline is the state's lowest ground at 571 feet. The Census Bureau measures about 549 square miles of land. The River Raisin and Sandy Creek drain it. French settlers reached Frenchtown on the Raisin in the 1780s, and the county was carved out in 1817.

A few features color what buyers see:

  • The city of Monroe is both county seat and largest city, and Dundee drew attention in 2001 when a large Cabela's store opened there.
  • Nine public school districts operate within the county, and its district-of-choice policy lets a family enroll in any district with room.
  • Industry marks the lakeshore. The Port of Monroe is still heavily industrial, and the Enrico Fermi nuclear station sits in Frenchtown Charter Township near the water.
  • Monroe County Community College is the only higher education campus in the county.
  • Lake Erie Transit runs eight fixed routes in and around the city of Monroe.

Tornadoes are uncommon, about 30 since 1950, and the latest with significant damage hit Dundee Township in June 2010.

Do the county's boundary quirks affect any deeds?

A few do, which is why a legal description matters more here than a street address. The Toledo War settlement of 1836 left a sliver of Monroe County, the Lost Peninsula in Erie Township, separated from the rest of Michigan by the state line, and most of that land is a marina. A 1973 agreement then ran the line through tiny Turtle Island in Lake Erie, giving Erie Township the Michigan half.

Lakeshore and river parcels raise their own questions about bottomland and easements. If your house touches Lake Erie, the River Raisin or Sandy Creek, hand the title company your survey and any earlier easements at the start, so the exceptions on the title commitment are known well before the buyer's deadline.

How do the Census figures describe Monroe County homes?

The Bureau's 2025 estimate is 156,004 people in 67,494 housing units. Owners hold 81.7 percent of homes. Half of owner-occupied houses sit above $228,900 in the 2020-2024 data, and renters pay a median $1,059. Household income has a median of $77,335. Commuters travel 26.2 minutes on average, and building permits totaled 191 in 2025. Density was 281.8 people per square mile in 2020.

The county has 63,029 households averaging 2.45 people. Nine in ten residents stayed at the same address over the prior year, 23.3 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 9.7 percent of residents are in poverty. Set beside Midland County, the middle Monroe County house is worth about $33,500 more, and owners make up 3.6 points more of the households.

More questions about Monroe County, MI Register of Deeds

What hours does the Monroe County deeds office keep?

Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Anything real property related that comes in after 3:00 p.m. is recorded or filed the following working day.

How much is the flat charge for a deed there?

$30 per document regardless of length. Extra instruments assigned or discharged add $3 each, and certifying a copy adds $5. Plain copies of real estate records are $1 a page, and the warranty deed tax certificate is a separate charge.

Does the office search by property address?

No. It cannot search ownership by address and needs a grantor or grantee name plus an approximate year. The Equalization Department or a city assessor can supply the name on the tax roll.

Which transfer tax rates does the county list?

$1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state, based on total consideration. A $200,000 sale comes to $1,720, with $1,500 to the state and $220 to the county.

How can I pay at the counter?

Cash, checks and credit cards are accepted. A card carries a 3 percent fee with a $2 minimum, so a check costs less on a large closing.

Which office files deeds for Oakland County land?

The combined Clerk/Register of Deeds handles them. Land record questions can go to the office by phone at 248-858-0597 or by email to deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov. Walk-in service is weekdays only, from 8:30 a.m. through the late afternoon. Almost 100 employees work in the combined office, which serves roughly 1.2 million residents and ranks among the biggest in Michigan.

Oakland County dates to 1820, and the office keeps documents from that period. Michigan counties rarely merge the two offices, but Oakland did so in 1958. Staff record more than 140,000 real estate documents every year.

The county has 530,460 households and 569,537 housing units. Census data shows 89.1% of residents kept the same address through the prior year, and median monthly owner costs are $1,998 with a mortgage against $778 without. Mortgages and discharges therefore pass through the recording counter next to deeds.

The public record spans deeds, mortgages, foreclosure records and personal property filings. The Oakland County Super Index supplies copies of recorded documents from 1964 forward, except subdivision plats. As of November 3, 2025 the office stopped recording UCC filings apart from land records, so land record fees cover them.

Not every records request belongs at the deeds counter. The Register of Deeds does not issue birth certificates or other vital records, and it does not take UCC filings for utility transfers. The wider Clerk's office keeps circuit court documents, military discharge forms and birth, death and marriage records for the county, so route those questions to the Clerk instead of the land records staff.

What does the Oakland County register collect when a deed is filed?

One deed carries a flat $30 charge, whatever its length. Of that, $4.00 is the state survey and remonumentation charge. The same $30 base amount appears in Michigan's fee statute, MCL 600.2567.

How much does transfer tax add to an Oakland County sale?

Any written transfer of real property worth $100 or more is taxed. Oakland's county rate works out to $1.10 for every $1,000 of price and the state rate to $7.50. A claimed exemption must be explained on the document.

Using the county's $343,600 median home value, the county portion is about $378 and the state portion about $2,577, which makes roughly $2,955. Recording depends on meeting the signature and format rules of MCL 565.201, Michigan's recording statute. Staff examine each one and record only those that pass, and a validation unit checks the legal description before the cashier takes the document.

  • The names in the notary block match the names under the signatures.
  • Any instrument that conveys or encumbers real estate shows the grantee's name and address.
  • A document signed in Michigan carries a notary acknowledgment listing the notary's county of commission and expiration date.
  • Black ink, type of at least 10 points, and white paper of 20-pound weight, sized from letter to legal length.
  • An unprinted band of 2.5 inches opens the first page, with half an inch left clear elsewhere.
  • The first printed line names the recordable event.
  • Total property value is given on the document or an affidavit.

When a document names a survivor, a certified death certificate or proof of death must go with it. A court order has to carry the court clerk's certification and seal. Older instruments follow the rules of their day: male grantors' marital status was required before April 6, 2017, and two witnesses before March 2002.

Can Oakland County documents be recorded electronically?

Yes. Four registered providers connect to the register: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and HopDox. UCC documents and mortgage foreclosure documents cannot be e-recorded.

The county also runs MiPropDocs for documents that do not transfer ownership. It accepts affidavits, association liens and discharges, claims of lien, certificates of trust, discharges, lis pendens, mortgages, notices of commencement, releases and satisfactions of mortgage. Deeds cannot use it, so a house transfer still goes through a provider account or on paper.

Paper filings remain open to anyone. Bring the original to the counter or mail it with payment. Copy the legal description from the prior deed word for word, since the validation step reviews it.

How do the register and the county treasurer work together on a sale?

The tax certificate is where the two offices meet. The treasurer confirms the parcel is paid up before a warranty deed goes on record, and the register will not file the deed without the stamp. To price a delinquent balance in advance, buy an official statement through the county's Property Gateway.

Tax foreclosure reaches the register too. It collects redemption money for sheriff deeds and clerk deeds, checks the person redeeming has a stake in the parcel, and passes the funds to the treasurer, who holds them in trust until the paperwork is finished and a check can go to the grantee. Anyone who inherited a house with unpaid taxes should read the Oakland County property tax guide before listing, since the county's foreclosure calendar runs on fixed dates.

How soon does a recorded deed come back?

A document carried to the counter returns in roughly two weeks. One sent by mail takes two to four. A document that came through a title company usually returns about two weeks after recording. Originals are indexed and then mailed back.

Copy requests move faster. Counter customers get five pages as a courtesy, and bigger orders are usually ready within a day or two, for pickup or mailing. The office can quote a foreclosure payoff and takes redemptions on sheriff deeds and clerk deeds from parties with a stake in the land. Money for a redemption is receipted and held by the treasurer until paperwork is complete.

$30 per document, whatever its length. The $4.00 state survey and remonumentation charge is part of that. A discharge that covers several instruments adds $3.00 per extra reference.

Yes. Warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a warranty clause need the county treasurer's certification, at $5.00, before the register records them.

To January 1, 1964, apart from subdivision plat maps. Call the Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597 about anything older.

Are UCC statements still filed separately in Oakland County?

No. After November 3, 2025 they are handled with land records, and the land record recording fees apply.

The seller or grantor, under the Michigan acts, paid with the recording. Combined county and state tax in Oakland County is about $8.60 per $1,000 of the sale price.

The archive reaches into the late 1800s. Anything from 1985 forward is electronic, and older material is on microfiche. New filings show up online within five days. Each one is time stamped, checked, numbered, indexed and scanned.

All real estate records are public, and anyone may search them in the office or online. Searches go by the property owner's name, and several public computers sit in the office. The staff do not run title searches. They send people to a title company or a private searcher. The county's view is that ownership follows whatever documents the office has recorded, so a seller with an old unrecorded deed in a drawer should file it before listing.

Online tools come in three flavors. Fidlar Laredo is a subscription program with a software download, popular for heavy searching. Fidlar Tapestry bills as you go and spans several Michigan counties. A free direct search link also exists on the county page.

Property Fraud Alert costs county landowners nothing and starts at 1-800-728-3858 or propertyfraudalert.com/mioscoda. It alerts you right away when a paper is recorded against your parcel. The county page adds that the Youngblood Law, House Bills 5598 and 5599, signed in November 2024, makes filing a fraudulent document with any Michigan register of deeds a felony.

What must a deed show before the Mio office accepts it?

The office drafts nothing and keeps no legal forms. It recommends an attorney or title company, and for do-it-yourselfers it names MichiganLegalHelp.org and eforms.com as starting places. Staff cannot say how a deed should be prepared.

MCL 565.201 governs the page itself: dark ink signatures with printed names, the grantee's address, the drafter's name and address, and a 2.5 inch clear top margin on the first page. MCL 211.135 governs tax proof. Before a warranty deed records, the county treasurer certifies that no liens or tax titles are held and that five years of taxes are paid. A quitclaim without warranty covenants is excused. Get the certificate from the Oscoda County Treasurer and carry it with the deed to Mio.

What is selling a house in Oscoda County like?

Oscoda County is the only county in Michigan with no incorporated city or village. Mio, the seat, is a census-designated place in the Au Sable River valley, where M-33 and M-72 meet. The south half lies in the Huron National Forest, much of it on the Grayling outwash plain of sandy ridges, jack pine and hardwoods. Neighbors include Montmorency, Alpena, Alcona, Iosco, Ogemaw, Roscommon, Crawford and Otsego counties. The legislature created the county in 1840 and its government formed in 1881. The name is a Schoolcraft coinage thought to mean pebbly prairie.

The 2020 census counted 8,219 people, the fewest of any Lower Peninsula county. The Bureau estimates 8,723 for July 2025, up 6.1% from 2020. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a middle home value of $125,500, owner occupancy of 87.2%, and monthly rent of $681. Household income is $49,515, and about one in three residents is 65 or older. Only 44.1% of residents 16 and older are in the labor force, and the average commute is 29.1 minutes.

The Census Bureau's snapshot of residents adds useful context for anyone pricing a house here:

  • 16.8% of people under 65 live with a disability, and 16.5% of residents are in poverty.
  • 81.4% of households have a broadband subscription, so remote-work buyers should confirm service at a given address.
  • 85.9% of adults 25 and older finished high school, and 15.6% hold a bachelor's degree.
  • 90.5% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

With no city or village government anywhere in the county, the county offices in Mio are the nearest local government for every parcel. Oscoda County Park is listed as a good vantage point over the area. The work economy is small: the Bureau counts 176 employer establishments with 1,335 jobs in 2023, up 6.2% from 2022, and 2022 retail sales of $72.2 million. Housing units total 7,792 against 3,788 households, which shows how many homes sit empty or are used seasonally. The Bureau tallied 24 building permits in 2025. Before listing a cabin or woodland home, search the owner's name at the register and ask the county treasurer for the tax certificate, since both steps affect closing speed.

More questions about Oscoda County, MI Register of Deeds

Where is the Oscoda County register's office?

It is at 311 South Morenci Avenue in Mio, MI 48647. Letters go to PO Box 399, and the main number is 989-826-1110.

Does Oscoda County take deeds by mail?

Yes. Send the original to the PO Box, or ship by UPS or FedEx to the street address, and include a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return.

Which e-recording vendors does Oscoda County use?

CSC Ingeo, EPN and Simplifile. Certified court documents and death certificates are excluded, so call before sending one.

What does a $100,000 Oscoda County sale owe in transfer tax?

It is $860: $750 for the state and $110 for the county, if no exemption fits. A partial $500 block counts as a full one, so a price just over a block boundary adds to the bill.

Does the Mio office search titles?

No. It is a recording office and refers people to title companies or private searchers, though you may search names yourself in the office or online.

Who records property documents in Otsego County, Michigan?

Find the Otsego County Register of Deeds at 225 W Main Street, Gaylord, MI 49735. Call 989-731-7550 or fax 989-731-7519. By the county's own description, this office keeps every record of a transfer or encumbrance of land in Otsego County.

Staff time stamp each paper, assign liber and page numbers and index it on computer. The computerized index and images start on March 5, 1864, and every record can be pulled and copied in the office within minutes. Images are also sold online.

The office works with the county Equalization Department to keep ownership current, using tax identification numbers or owner names. It does not run searches for the public. Anyone who wants a search done on their behalf should call a title insurance company or a land records data company, or sit at the Gaylord counter and look for themselves.

What does recording cost in Gaylord?

The Gaylord office charges $30 for each document it records, with every page included. The county says that rate took effect October 1, 2016. The table below comes straight from the county's fee and copies pages.

Otsego County Register of Deeds fees, from otsegocountymi.gov

Per the county, $4 of the fee is routed to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation Fund, a share that is skipped for fixture filings, state, federal and MESC liens, state deeds and plats. For mailed copy orders, phone 989-731-7551 first so staff can fix the page count and price. Payment is due when the service is performed, and checks are made out to Otsego County Register of Deeds.

How do transfer tax and exemptions work in Otsego County?

The clerk's staff collect transfer tax at the moment of recording, and the county's page cites MCL 207.505(5) and MCL 207.526(6) for it. Either print the full consideration on the deed or file a real estate transfer valuation affidavit, at no charge. An exempt transfer should say so on its face.

The rates are $3.75 for the state and 55 cents for the county per $500 or fraction. They come from MCL 207.525 and MCL 207.504. A sale at $220,000, matching the $219,700 middle home value reported for Otsego County, is 440 blocks of $500. State tax is $1,650 and county tax is $242, so $1,892 is due at recording unless an exemption applies.

Exemptions that matter to homeowners:

  • Consideration below $100 removes the tax under both acts.
  • A deed from a mortgage foreclosure skips the state tax, and one given on a government-backed loan skips both. The state exemption does not carry over to the lender's later sale of the property.
  • Deeds within a family, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, are exempt from the state tax only.
  • A land contract owes nothing until the buyer finishes paying and legal title passes.
  • A deed that moves a boundary line with no money paid is exempt from both.

Mineral rights transfers and leases are exempt too, but they come up rarely in a house sale.

Can I e-record or search Otsego County land records online?

Yes. Otsego County offers electronic recording for people who file many documents at once. It is a secure, verified-user service, and you register through an approved provider before you start. The county names Simplifile, at simplifile.com, and CSC, at cscglobal.com/service/erecording.

Online, the office sells images of recorded documents. Searching the real estate record at the office costs $5 per name, and certificate searches for state tax liens, federal tax liens and U.C.C.-11 filings carry the per-name fees in the table above.

Freedom of Information requests go on a completed FOIA Request Form sent by email to the county's FOIA coordinator or faxed to 989-731-7529. A deed copy does not need a FOIA request, since recorded instruments are available at $1 per page.

What paperwork should a deed carry before it reaches the Gaylord counter?

The Gaylord office applies two statutes. MCL 565.201 governs how the paper looks, and MCL 211.135 governs proof that taxes are paid. A deed that misses either can be refused.

  • Legible black or dark blue signatures, with each signer's name printed below and matching the notary's wording.
  • The grantee's mailing address, plus whoever drafted the instrument with a business address.
  • Black type of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, between letter and legal size, and a clear 2.5 inches at the top of page one.
  • A single opening line naming the one recordable event, such as a warranty deed or a mortgage discharge.
  • Social Security numbers masked down to the last four digits, unless a law demands more.

With a covenant of warranty in the deed, the county treasurer must certify there are no tax liens or titles on the parcel and that five prior years of taxes are paid. A city, village or township treasurer certifies the local side. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants, a sheriff's deed and a deed made under a court judgment are excused.

How does the Otsego County setting shape a house sale?

Otsego County spans 526 square miles of Northern Michigan, which makes it the fifth smallest in the state by total area. Gaylord is the only city and also the seat, with Vanderbilt as the lone village. Unincorporated communities include Elmira, Johannesburg, Waters, Sparr and the lakeside settlement of Otsego Lake. The county began as Okkuddo County in 1840, became Otsego in 1843, and organized in 1875.

Water shapes the housing stock. The county has more than 370 lakes, mostly in the south, and Otsego Lake is the largest at 1,972 acres. The headwaters of the Au Sable, Black, Manistee, Pigeon and Sturgeon rivers are here. I-75 bypasses Gaylord on the west and M-32 runs east and west through it.

The 2020 census counted 25,091 residents, and the Bureau's 2025 estimate is 26,080, a gain of 3.9%. For 2020 to 2024 it reports a $219,700 middle home value, 77.2% owner occupancy and a $1,008 monthly rent. Median household income is $68,183. The county has 14,976 housing units but 11,231 households, so housing units outnumber households by about 3,700. Building permits numbered 25 in 2025, and retail sales per resident in 2022 were $39,474, far above the other three counties in the same release.

The Census Bureau counts 846 employer establishments in Otsego County in 2023, with 9,372 jobs and a $448 million annual payroll. Retail sales topped $1 billion in 2022, and health care and social assistance receipts reached $213 million. Households with a broadband subscription make up 91.3%, and 26.3% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. A buyer who works remotely can find service, but should confirm it at the address.

Owners of lake or woodland parcels can ask the Equalization Department for the parcel's tax identification number, and the Treasurer for the tax certificate, before choosing a closing date.

Gaylord charges $30 a document with all pages included, and adds $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

None. The county collects nothing for the affidavit, which you can use instead of printing the value on the deed.

They start on March 5, 1864. The office keeps both the index and the images on computer from that date to the present.

Each page is $1, and a certification adds $5. For mail orders, ring the office first for an exact quote.

Which Ottawa County office records my deed, and where is it?

The Register of Deeds pages list Room 146 as the recording office, and the county's locations page shows a combined vital records and deeds counter in Room 130 of the same building, so phone ahead at (616) 994-4510 to learn which window takes your deed. The email is register@miottawa.org and the fax is (616) 994-4521.

A second site, the Research Library, is at 414 Washington Avenue, Room 115, in Grand Haven, the county seat. Its direct line is (616) 846-8109. Weekday service at both sites starts at 8 am and ends at 5 pm, though Grand Haven shuts for an hour after noon. Since January 1, 2026 the vital records and deeds offices close from 8:00 to 9:30 am on the third Monday of each month.

A big county needs several doors. Ottawa County counts 296,200 residents, and the Clerk and Register of Deeds operates five locations. Only West Olive and Grand Haven handle deeds, while Holland and Hudsonville are vital records sites.

How does recording work in Ottawa County?

Ottawa County records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt, as long as it meets the recording requirements. A fax or photocopy of a deed is turned away, because originals with live signatures are all it accepts. Court papers must be certified by the court, and a death certificate must be certified by the Clerk's office before it can be recorded.

Professional filers use electronic recording. The county's software lets it record warranty deeds and other documents that need a tax stamp, and it accepts submissions from four approved companies, including Indecomm, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. Contact each firm about eligibility and pricing. The county's business rules say the office collects only the fees set by state and local law, and vendors may add processing charges.

A one-time filer can use the Consumer E-Recording portal for affidavits, liens, certificates of trust, mortgages, discharges, lis pendens, notices of commencement and releases. Deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are barred from the consumer portal, so a seller has to deliver the deed in paper or through a title company.

At the counter you can pay in cash, by check or by card. Recording by card adds a 3% convenience fee, and copy orders can also draw on an escrow account.

Michigan sets the base amounts in MCL 600.2567, and Ottawa County posts its own online and card terms in its FAQ and document search pages. Searching the index is free, and the county asks $1 per page, plus a convenience fee, to view, print or save an image.

Ottawa County fees from the Register of Deeds FAQ and document search, and the state schedule in MCL 600.2567
ItemAmount

The county's FAQ says documents are not obtained through Freedom of Information requests, since every record in the office is public or covered by statute and copy fees are fixed by state law. Anyone can obtain a copy of your deed once it is recorded.

How much transfer tax will an Ottawa County seller pay?

Two statutes stack here: MCL 207.525 levies $3.75 per $500 for the state, and MCL 207.504 levies 55 cents per $500 for the county, which is the rate for any county under 2,000,000 people. Any remainder under $500 is treated as a full block.

The median owner-occupied home in Ottawa County is valued at $323,400, the highest of the four counties in this release. On a $325,000 sale there are 650 blocks of $500. State tax comes to $2,437.50 and county tax to $357.50, a total of $2,795 at recording. The deed needs to show the value or carry an affidavit.

You can often avoid the tax with an exemption written on the deed. The common ones for homeowners are:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • Mortgage foreclosure deeds, including deeds in lieu, under the state act.
  • Gifts down the family line, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which the state act alone excuses.
  • A spouse's deed that makes or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A deed whose only job is to cure a flaw in title the grantee already holds.

The county site links both a County Exemptions sheet and a State Exemptions sheet on its Document Recording page.

What do I need to prepare before recording an Ottawa County deed?

The office does not draft documents, supply forms or give legal advice, and it does not furnish abstracts of title. It suggests an attorney, title company or real estate agent for help. It cannot say when a house was built or whether a survey exists either, since it only holds land records, and most property has never had a survey recorded.

Ottawa County explains its top margin rule this way: a state law effective April 1, 1997 requires 2.5 inches at the top and half an inch on the other sides, to leave room for recording stamps. MCL 565.201 contains that rule. Witnesses are no longer required on documents, though most documents still need a notary.

Papers that need a tax certificate from the Treasurer's office:

  • Warranty deeds.
  • Land contracts and assignments of land contracts.
  • Master deeds and amendments to master deeds.

MCL 211.135 backs that requirement and excuses quitclaim deeds without covenants of warranty. If a house is in mortgage foreclosure, the Register of Deeds takes redemption payments, though you may redeem straight through the lender or its lawyer. After the redemption period runs out, only the lender can help.

The county also offers Property Fraud Alerts. Owners sign up to be told when a document is recorded that affects their property.

What is selling a house in Ottawa County like?

Ottawa County is in West Michigan on 24 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. Its 1,631 square miles include 1,068 of water, so only 563 are land. The Grand River, the longest in Michigan, crosses the county and empties into the lake at Grand Haven. Holland is the largest city, and the others include Zeeland, Hudsonville, Coopersville and Ferrysburg. Grand Valley State University is in Allendale and Hope College is in Holland. The county was authorized in 1831 and organized in 1837.

School districts that serve the county include Grand Haven Area Public Schools, Holland City School District, West Ottawa, Zeeland Public Schools, Hudsonville Public School District, Spring Lake Public Schools, Jenison Public Schools and Allendale Public School District.

The Census Bureau counted 296,200 people in 2020 and estimates 308,459 in July 2025, up 4.1%. For 2020 to 2024 it lists a median home value of $323,400, an owner-occupied rate of 79.3%, median gross rent of $1,211 and median household income of $90,502. The Bureau recorded 1,411 building permits in 2025, many more than in the three northern counties.

Bring it to the recording office at 12220 Fillmore Street in West Olive, or let a title company e-record it. Phone (616) 994-4510 to confirm the room. The Washington Avenue site in Grand Haven is the research library.

Can I record a photocopy or fax of a deed in Ottawa County?

No. Staff record only papers bearing original signatures.

How quickly does Ottawa County record a deed?

The county says it records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt when it meets the recording requirements. A title company or lender decides when the original reaches you.

Can I use the Ottawa County consumer e-recording portal for my deed?

No. The portal excludes deeds and other documents that transfer ownership, as well as UCC documents and foreclosure papers. It handles items like mortgages, discharges and notices of commencement.

What would a $400,000 Ottawa County sale owe in transfer tax?

The bill is $3,440 with no exemption: $3,000 to the state and $440 to the county.
